## 391. 2026-09-27T02:56:41.376Z — endpoint_actual_bubbles

Research thread: `01a0e0a8-646e-78d3-938d-ddba97fef1d2`.

The bounded-sectional-curvature route works, and Cheeger–Tian strengthens it to a diameter-free theorem for exact Einstein metrics with bounded Euler density. The analogous bounded-Ricci extension remains unverified.

### 1. Local exponential averaging

For the defect \(Z_t\) of §8, fix \(K,L>0\), \(t\in[0,1/4]\), and
\[
4a<\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{\max\{K,1\}}}.
\]
If \(\omega\) is self-dual, \(|\omega|\le L\), and
\[
G_{K,a}=\{x:|\sec|\le K\text{ throughout }B_{4a}(x)\},
\]
then
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Vol}G_{K,a}}V
 \le C(K,L,a)\fint Z_t. \tag{1}
\]

For \(x\in G_{K,a}\), pull back by \(\exp_x\) to the tangent ball \(B_{4a}\). It is nonsingular; its radial distance from the origin is \(|v|\), and its exponential map at the origin is the identity. The lifted metric therefore has uniform interior harmonic charts, independent of base injectivity. These facts require no curvature derivatives. [Normal-cover propositions 2.6–2.7](https://academic.oup.com/imrn/article/2026/14/rnag158/8733970).

The §8 compactness argument on a fixed interior chart gives
\[
E_a(x):=\int_{|v|<a}Z_t(\exp_xv)\,d\mu_{\exp_x^*g}\ge\varepsilon_{\rm loc}>0.
\]
Indeed, failure gives the same smooth limit
\[
\operatorname{Ric}=-g,\quad d\omega=0,\quad |\omega|^2=2,
\quad W^+=t(2I/3-\omega\otimes\omega).
\]
For \(t=0\), Armstrong excludes it locally; for \(t>0\), Bianchi implies \(\nabla\omega=0\), forcing \(t=1/2\).

Rauch bounds the polar Jacobian by \(C(K,a)s^3\). Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{\rm loc}\operatorname{Vol}G_{K,a}
&\le C(K,a)\int_0^a s^3
 \int_{G_{K,a}}\int_{S_xM}Z_t(\exp_x(s\theta))\,d\theta\,d\mu(x)\,ds\\
&\le C(K,a)|S^3|\frac{a^4}{4}\int_M Z_t .
\end{aligned}
\]
The last equality after dropping the center restriction follows from preservation of Liouville measure by geodesic flow. No sheet bound or regular-cover assumption occurs.

For the actual supplier, this proves
\[
|\sec|\le K,\quad\beta\ge4
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
r_{\rm Ric}+D_\beta/V\ge c(K)>0.
\]
More generally, its sectional-curvature radius tends to zero in measure along any hypothetical zero-defect sequence.

### 2. Exact Einstein: Euler density suffices

Use curvature-operator norm and suppose
\[
\operatorname{Ric}=-g,\qquad
\Lambda=\fint|\mathcal R|^2=\frac{8\pi^2\chi(M)}V\le\Lambda_0.
\]

Cheeger–Tian gives universal \(\varepsilon_{\rm CT},C_{\rm CT}>0\):
\[
\int_{B_R(x)}|\mathcal R|^2\le\varepsilon_{\rm CT}
\Longrightarrow
\sup_{B_{R/2}(x)}|\mathcal R|\le C_{\rm CT}R^{-2},
\qquad 0<R\le1.
\]
This is explicitly an unnormalized, collapse-independent estimate. Fixed norm-conversion factors are absorbed in its constants. [Cheeger’s author statement, slides 2–3](https://sites.duke.edu/scshgap/files/2016/08/dim4dukebeamer.pdf).

Bishop comparison and Fubini give
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Vol}\{x:\int_{B_R(x)}|\mathcal R|^2>
\varepsilon_{\rm CT}\}}V
 \le C_0\Lambda R^4.
\]
The complementary centers satisfy the hypotheses of (1), with \(K=C/R^2\), \(a=\theta R\). Therefore
\[
1\le C_0\Lambda R^4+C_1(R)\fint Z_t
 \le C_0\Lambda R^4+C_2(R)\kappa. \tag{2}
\]
Choosing \(R=R(\Lambda_0)>0\) makes the first term at most \(1/2\). Thus
\[
\boxed{D_\beta/V\ge\varepsilon(\Lambda_0)>0,\qquad\beta\ge4.}
\]
No diameter, volume, noncollapse, or class-square assumption is needed. Exact Einstein is essential to the verified argument. In particular, exact-Einstein zero-end degeneration requires \(\chi/V\to\infty\).

### 3. Uniform upper-wall consequence

Assume additionally \(T_+=A(1-h)\), \(p\ge A\), and \(\chi/A\le B\). The scalar bound gives \(e\ge p/A\ge1\), hence \(\Lambda\le4B\). Set
\[
\varepsilon=\min\{1,\varepsilon(4B)\}.
\]
For every \(h\in[1/4,1/3]\),
\[
\boxed{e\le G(h)-\varepsilon^2/288.} \tag{3}
\]

To verify the uniform constant, put \(a_h=3(1-h)\), \(d=a_h-e\), and \(\delta=G(h)-e\). If \(\beta_*=\sqrt{8e/d}\ge4\), optimizing the pencil gives
\[
\varepsilon e\le P(e)
:=14e+2a_h-36+8\sqrt{2e(a_h-e)}.
\]
Since \(P(G)=0\), \(G\le9/4\), and
\(e(a_h-e)\le G(a_h-G)+G\delta\),
\[
\varepsilon\le\varepsilon e\le12\sqrt{2\delta}.
\]
If \(\beta_*<4\), instead \(\delta\ge4/9\), stronger than (3).

Also, with
\[
\beta_c=\frac{14-\varepsilon+\sqrt{(14-\varepsilon)^2+128}}4,
\]
the pencil at \(\beta_c\) yields
\[
h\le1-\frac6{\beta_c+1}
\le\frac13-\frac{8\varepsilon}{243}.
\]

For the inherited actual complex-hyperbolic surgery families,
\[
\frac{\chi(M)}A=\frac13+\frac{k}A-\frac{2\ell}A
\le\frac13+h\le\frac23.
\]
Thus one absolute \(\varepsilon_*=\min\{1,\varepsilon(8/3)\}\) applies throughout this window. The substantive improvement is the nonvanishing margin through \(h=1/4\).

### 4. Bounded-Ricci extension: precise missing input

I did not verify a published implication from bounded Ricci plus small unnormalized local \(L^2\) curvature to the required regular local cover. Cheeger’s slide 5 is qualitative and does not specify the necessary covering/radius hypotheses.

The verified alternative, [Naber–Zhang Proposition 6.4](https://arxiv.org/html/1412.1326#S6.SS2), additionally requires GH model closeness and maximal fibered-fundamental-group rank. It then supplies harmonic charts on local universal covers without \(\nabla\operatorname{Ric}\) bounds. Small base curvature energy has not been shown here to imply those extra hypotheses. Accordingly, the approximate-Einstein Euler-density theorem remains unclaimed.

No files changed.

## 392. 2026-09-27T03:03:24.135Z — zero_endpoint_system_20260927

Research thread: `01a0e086-9e15-7e60-8e58-fc4cb8d820b9`.

The construction is valid. The only correction is terminological: the squared Hessian \(L^2\) energy is \(O(\epsilon^2)\); its \(L^2\) norm is \(O(\epsilon)\). It gives exact local positive-weight solutions, without prescribed boundary matching.

### Right inverses and contraction

Work on the fixed Euclidean ball \(\Omega=B_2\), using \(\Delta=-\sum_j\partial_j^2\). Fix \(k\ge2\), \(0<\alpha<1\), \(a>0\), and \(f_*>0\).

Let \(G_D\) be the componentwise Dirichlet inverse of \(\Delta\). On the fixed smooth ball,
\[
G_D:C^{k,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)
 \longrightarrow C^{k+2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)
\]
is bounded. These are the usual boundary Schauder estimates; [Viaclovsky’s lectures 11–17](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-156-differential-analysis-spring-2004/pages/lecture-notes/) supply the classical analytic input.

For \(T=(d^*,\sqrt2d^+)\),
\[
TT^*=\Delta I_{\Lambda^0\oplus\Lambda^+}.
\]
Indeed, the off-diagonal terms vanish, while for a self-dual two-form \(\eta\),
\[
2d^+d^*\eta=dd^*\eta+d^*d\eta=\Delta\eta.
\]
Thus \(R_A=T^*G_D\) is a right inverse, gaining one derivative. Likewise,
\[
D^+D^-=\Delta I_{S^-},\qquad R_D=D^-G_D,
\]
so \(D^+R_D=I\), also with one derivative gained.

Put \(\lambda=\epsilon^2\) and
\[
g(y)=\frac{\bar z_1^2-\bar z_2^2}{4},\qquad
\Phi_0=ae_1+\epsilon ge_2 .
\]
Direct Clifford calculation gives \(D^+\Phi_0=0\). Define
\[
A_\lambda(\Phi)
 =R_A(0,\sqrt2\lambda i f_*\sigma(\Phi)),\qquad
\mathcal F_\lambda(\Phi)
 =\Phi_0-\frac12R_D[c(A_\lambda(\Phi))\Phi].
\]

Treat \(C^{k,\alpha}(\overline\Omega;\mathbb C^2)\) as a real Banach space. On any fixed bounded ball,
\[
\|A_\lambda(\Phi)\|_{k+1,\alpha}\le C\lambda\|\Phi\|_{k,\alpha}^2,
\]
\[
\|\mathcal F_\lambda(\Phi)-\Phi_0\|_{k,\alpha}\le C_M\lambda,
\qquad
\|\mathcal F_\lambda(\Phi)-\mathcal F_\lambda(\Psi)\|_{k,\alpha}
 \le C_M\lambda\|\Phi-\Psi\|_{k,\alpha}.
\]
Hence, for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), it is a contraction on
\(\|\Phi-\Phi_0\|_{k,\alpha}\le C_0\lambda\). Its fixed point satisfies exactly
\[
D_A\Phi=0,\qquad d^*A=0,\qquad
F_A^+=\lambda i f_*\sigma(\Phi),
\]
and
\[
A=O(\epsilon^2),\qquad \Phi-\Phi_0=O(\epsilon^2)
\]
in the indicated Hölder norms. Bootstrapping gives smoothness and the same order in every fixed higher norm.

Importantly, zero Dirichlet data are imposed on the auxiliary Poisson potentials—not on \(A\) or \(\Phi-\Phi_0\). No boundary matching theorem is implicit here.

### Physical scaling and actual torsion

On \(B_{2\epsilon}\), define
\[
\widehat\Phi(x)=\Phi(x/\epsilon),\qquad
\widehat A_j(x)=\epsilon^{-1}A_j(x/\epsilon).
\]
Then exactly
\[
D_{\widehat A}\widehat\Phi=0,\qquad
F_{\widehat A}^+=i f_*\sigma(\widehat\Phi),\qquad
d^*\widehat A=0.
\]
In rescaled \(y\)-coordinates,
\[
\rho=a^2+O(\epsilon^2),\quad
\zeta=O(\epsilon),\quad P=O(1),\quad H=O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]

Central connection terms disappear from \(\Phi\wedge P_i\). For the seed, direct calculation gives
\[
t_{\Phi_0}=a^2(\bar z_1,\bar z_2).
\]
Consequently the actual physical torsion satisfies
\[
\widehat t(\epsilon y)
 =a^2(\bar z_1,\bar z_2)+O(\epsilon)
 \quad\text{in }C^1(\overline B_2).
\]

There is a useful strengthening: the fixed point \(\Phi\) is even and \(A\) is odd. The Dirichlet inverse preserves parity, while \(T^*\) and \(D^-\) reverse it. Therefore \(t\) is odd and vanishes exactly at the center. For small \(\epsilon\),
\[
|t(\epsilon y)-t(\epsilon y')|
 \ge(a^2-C\epsilon)|y-y'|.
\]
It is injective on \(B_2\), so this is its unique zero. Its real Jacobian has positive determinant, since the limiting determinant is \(a^8>0\).

### Curvature, signed flux, and critical concentration

Writing \(\sigma_0=\sigma(ae_1)\), the constant-source Dirichlet calculation gives
\[
A_y=\epsilon^2 A_0+O(\epsilon^3),\qquad
A_0=\frac{i f_*}{2}\,\iota_y\sigma_0.
\]
Thus
\[
F_{\widehat A}=i f_*\sigma_0+O(\epsilon),\qquad
F_{\widehat A}^-=O(\epsilon),
\]
and, with the project’s exterior-algebra norm,
\[
\int_{B_{2\epsilon}}|F_{\widehat A}|^2
 =\pi^2f_*^2a^4\epsilon^4+O(\epsilon^5).
\]
Also
\[
\int|H|^2=O(\epsilon^2),\qquad
\int|\nabla t|^2=O(\epsilon^2).
\]

Choose \(0<m_1<m_2<4a^4\) and a smooth cutoff \(\chi(m)\), equal to one below \(m_1\) and zero above \(m_2\). For small \(\epsilon\), its support avoids the outer boundary. The relative Chern identity, with the manuscript’s transgression sign, is
\[
1=\int\chi(m)c_2(F_{E_-})+\int d\chi(m)\wedge T_t .
\]
Here the flat-background connection on \(E_-=S^-\otimes L\) has curvature
\[
F_{E_-}=\frac32F_{\widehat A}I,\qquad
c_2(F_{E_-})=-\frac9{16\pi^2}F_{\widehat A}\wedge F_{\widehat A}.
\]
Its density is uniformly bounded, so
\[
\boxed{\int d\chi(m)\wedge T_t=1+O(\epsilon^4)>0.}
\]

The transition energies are stronger than merely \(O(1)\). On
\(T_\epsilon=\{m_1<|t|^2<m_2\}\),
\[
\boxed{\lim_{\epsilon\to0}
 \int_{T_\epsilon}|\langle t,\nabla t\rangle|^2|\nabla t|^2
 =\frac{8\pi^2}{3}(m_2^3-m_1^3)>0,}
\]
\[
\lim_{\epsilon\to0}\int_{T_\epsilon}|\nabla t|^4
 =8\pi^2(m_2^2-m_1^2).
\]
These follow by rescaling: the limiting torsion has
\(m=a^4|y|^2\), \(|dt|^2=4a^4\), and
\(|\langle t,dt\rangle|^2=2a^8|y|^2\).

### Exact scope

For the flat metric, \(s=W^+=0\), hence the canonical weight is exactly
\[
f_0=\max\{\sqrt{\max(q,3)},(-s)_+/4\}=\sqrt3.
\]
Taking \(f_*=\sqrt3\) therefore satisfies the actual local curvature equation with the canonical weight. Taking \(a<2\) also retains the supplied amplitude bound \(\rho<4\).

This strengthens §14: positive torsion cutoff flux survives both actual local weighted equations, not merely their Dirac consequences. It does not supply a closed conformally solvable class, boundary matching, or a globally small normalized Einstein defect. Accordingly it blocks a local-equation-only cancellation argument, not a global endpoint theorem.

The project Skill influenced this scope distinction; no files were edited.

## 393. 2026-09-27T03:12:19.397Z — endpoint_actual_bubbles

Research thread: `01a0e0a8-646e-78d3-938d-ddba97fef1d2`.

No new topology-only exclusion near \(h=1/4\) follows from the inspected actual families and their recorded energy bounds.

The obstruction is directional: topology supplies
\[
e\le U=\frac{3\min(T_+,T_-)}A,
\]
not a lower bound near \(G(h)\). The Euler-density bound makes I42 uniform, but does not force a candidate into its forbidden upper strip.

A genuine family demonstrating the remaining numerical freedom is
\[
M_j=X_j\#k_j\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2},\qquad
k_j=\lceil A_j/4\rceil ,
\]
where \(X_j\) are increasingly large complex-hyperbolic covers and \(A_j=c_1^2(X_j)\). The inherited exceptional-sign theorem supplies actual classes with
\[
p_j\ge A_j,\qquad a_j^2=T_+(M_j)=A_j-k_j.
\]
Here
\[
h_j\to\tfrac14^+,\quad
\chi(M_j)/A_j\to\tfrac7{12},\quad
U_j\to\tfrac94.
\]

Nevertheless, the formal Einstein energy \(e=7/4\), with the minimum permitted projection budget \(p=A\), satisfies the recorded scalar and Chern–Weil constraints. At the limiting topology,
\[
\frac{\int|W^+|^2}{2\pi^2A}=\frac16,\qquad
\frac{\int|W^-|^2}{2\pi^2A}=1,\qquad
\Lambda=\frac43,
\]
and
\[
\inf_{\beta>0}\frac{D_\beta}{V}
=-4+\frac{16}{\sqrt7}>2.
\]
Thus it also satisfies the new uniform pencil gap while remaining \(1/2\) below \(G(1/4)=9/4\). This is a non-implication witness for the inequalities, not an Einstein construction.

More generally, near \(h=1/4\), the recorded lower walls remain strictly below the improved upper wall. For example, on \([1/4,7/24]\),
\[
L_{\rm old}(h)
=\max\{F(h)+\varepsilon_{\rm old}h^2,\ 1+(1+c_0)h\}
<\frac74<G(h)-\frac1{288}.
\]
Consequently, replacing \(G\) by I42’s \(G-c(B)\) does not make the numerical interval empty unless \(U<L_{\rm old}\) already supplied a lower-wall obstruction.

There is also an actual check on the I41 constant: \(c_0\le2/9\). LeBrun’s blow-up metrics have
\[
e\to1+h,\qquad \mathcal J\to\frac{4h}{1+h}.
\]
Substitution into I41 gives \(1+(11/9)h\ge1+(1+c_0)h\). This uses scalar-flat insertions and vanishing transition contributions in [LeBrun’s Theorem 4.3 proof](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0003068); it is a coefficient ceiling, not an optimality claim.

The other inspected supplies do not add the missing lower bound:

- Existing ordinary and BF exclusion families tune \(U\) toward the lower walls \(F\) or \(L_h\).
- Ordinary rank-one degree/entropy bounds are dominated by the scalar budget on the classical complex-base family.
- The recorded simply connected BF blocks with handles have free fundamental group, so maps to closed aspherical four-manifolds have degree zero.

Accordingly, I42 currently excludes an energy region for these actual smooth types, not an additional entire topology family near \(h=1/4\). A further independent lower-volume or lower-energy constraint is needed. No files changed.

## 394. 2026-09-27T03:13:04.108Z — torsion_signed_topology

Research thread: `01a0e0a8-30e6-7192-bde0-85bf5a1bc64f`.

The construction persists on a fixed negative Einstein background. There is no local geometric defect: the cores satisfy \(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\), \(W^\pm=0\), and the canonical weight is exactly \(f=2\).

Take a fixed hyperbolic metric \(g\) of sectional curvature \(-1/3\), a point \(p\), and sufficiently small geodesic balls about \(p\). In normal coordinates \(x=\varepsilon y\), put
\[
g_\varepsilon=\varepsilon^{-2}(\exp_p(\varepsilon\,\cdot))^*g.
\]
Explicitly,
\[
g_\varepsilon
=dr^2+\frac3{\varepsilon^2}
 \sinh^2\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon r}{\sqrt3}\right)g_{S^3},
\]
and in Cartesian coordinates,
\[
g_{\varepsilon,ij}
=\delta_{ij}+\frac{\varepsilon^2}{9}
 (|y|^2\delta_{ij}-y_i y_j)+O(\varepsilon^4).
\]
Thus, on \(\overline B_2\), for every fixed finite \(k\),
\[
\|g_\varepsilon-\delta\|_{C^{k,\alpha}}\le C_k\varepsilon^2.
\]
Choose the oriented orthonormal coframe obtained from the positive square root of \(g_\varepsilon\), and its spin lift. The frame perturbation and spin connection are \(O(\varepsilon^2)\) in the corresponding fixed norms. In these trivializations,
\[
D_\varepsilon^\pm-D_0^\pm
=O(\varepsilon^2)\partial+O(\varepsilon^2).                 \tag{1}
\]

The right inverses can be constructed without imposing unverified boundary conditions on the gauge fields themselves.

For forms, let
\[
\mathcal T_\varepsilon=(d^*_\varepsilon,\sqrt2\,d^+_\varepsilon),
\quad
\mathcal T_\varepsilon^*(u,\omega)=du+\sqrt2\,d^*_\varepsilon\omega.
\]
Its target is
\(\Omega^0\oplus\Lambda^+_{g_\varepsilon}\). The exact identity is
\[
\mathcal T_\varepsilon\mathcal T_\varepsilon^*
=\Delta_{g_\varepsilon}
\quad\text{on this target}.                              \tag{2}
\]
In particular \(2d^+d^*\omega=\Delta\omega\) for self-dual \(\omega\). Identify the self-dual target with its Euclidean counterpart using the chosen orthonormal coframe. The conjugated operator in (2) is
\[
L_{A,\varepsilon}
=\Delta_0+O(\varepsilon^2)\partial^2
       +O(\varepsilon^2)\partial+O(\varepsilon^2).
\]
Let \(G_0\) be the Euclidean componentwise Dirichlet Green operator. On \(C^{k,\alpha}\),
\[
G_{A,\varepsilon}
=G_0\bigl[I+(L_{A,\varepsilon}-\Delta_0)G_0\bigr]^{-1}
\]
exists by a Neumann series for small \(\varepsilon\). Restoring the self-dual identification, define
\[
R_{A,\varepsilon}
=\mathcal T_\varepsilon^*G_{A,\varepsilon}.
\]
It is a real right inverse and therefore preserves imaginary-valued data after complexification.

Similarly,
\[
L_{D,\varepsilon}=D_\varepsilon^+D_\varepsilon^-
=\Delta_0+O(\varepsilon^2)\partial^2
       +O(\varepsilon^2)\partial+O(\varepsilon^2).
\]
Its Dirichlet inverse \(G_{D,\varepsilon}\) exists by the same argument, and
\[
R_{D,\varepsilon}=D_\varepsilon^-G_{D,\varepsilon},
\qquad
D_\varepsilon^+R_{D,\varepsilon}=\operatorname{id}.         \tag{3}
\]
Both right inverses map \(C^{k,\alpha}\) boundedly to \(C^{k+1,\alpha}\), uniformly for small \(\varepsilon\), and differ from their Euclidean counterparts by \(O(\varepsilon^2)\). Dirichlet regularity for the second-order operators supplies smoothness up to \(\partial B_2\).

Use the earlier Clifford matrices and set
\[
\rho_0=\frac43,\quad a=\sqrt{\rho_0},\quad
g_0(y)=\frac{\bar z_1^2-\bar z_2^2}{4},\quad
\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}=a e_1+\varepsilon g_0 e_2.
\]
Here \(D_0^+\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}=0\), while (1) gives
\[
D_\varepsilon^+\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}=O(\varepsilon^2).
\]
Correct it to an exact background Dirac seed:
\[
\widehat\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}
=\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}
 -R_{D,\varepsilon}D_\varepsilon^+\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}.
\]
Then
\[
D_\varepsilon^+\widehat\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}=0,\qquad
\widehat\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}-\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}
=O(\varepsilon^2)
\]
in every fixed \(C^{k+1,\alpha}\) norm.

Put \(\lambda=\varepsilon^2\), and define
\[
A(\Phi)=R_{A,\varepsilon}
 \bigl(0,\sqrt2\,\lambda i\,2\,\sigma_{g_\varepsilon}(\Phi)\bigr).
\]
The fixed-point equation is
\[
\Phi=\widehat\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}
-\frac12R_{D,\varepsilon}
       [c_{g_\varepsilon}(A(\Phi))\Phi].                  \tag{4}
\]
On a \(C\lambda\)-ball about the corrected seed, the right side preserves the ball and has Lipschitz constant \(C\lambda<1/2\). This follows directly from the bounded right inverses, multiplication estimates, and the quadratic nature of \(\sigma\). Thus (4) gives exact smooth solutions
\[
D_{A_\varepsilon,g_\varepsilon}\Phi_\varepsilon=0,\qquad
F_{A_\varepsilon}^{+,g_\varepsilon}
=\varepsilon^2 i\,2\,\sigma_{g_\varepsilon}(\Phi_\varepsilon),
\qquad d^*_\varepsilon A_\varepsilon=0,
\]
with
\[
\|A_\varepsilon\|_{C^{k+1,\alpha}}
+\|\Phi_\varepsilon-\Phi_{0,\varepsilon}\|_{C^{k+1,\alpha}}
\le C_k\varepsilon^2.                                    \tag{5}
\]
Starting with \(k\ge2\), the equations and Dirichlet inverses successively gain derivatives, giving smoothness on the closed ball.

Rescale back to the fixed physical metric. Since
\[
D_{\mathrm{phys}}=\varepsilon^{-1}D_{g_\varepsilon},
\]
and curvature two-forms scale by \(\varepsilon^{-2}\), the physical fields satisfy
\[
\boxed{\quad
D_{A,g}\Phi=0,\qquad F_A^+=i\,2\,\sigma_g(\Phi).
\quad}                                                    \tag{6}
\]
The physical metric remains the original fixed hyperbolic metric. Hence
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g=-g,\quad s=-4,\quad W^\pm=0
\]
exactly. Moreover \(q=-s+\sqrt6|W^+|=4\), so the prescribed canonical majorant is indeed
\[
f_0=\max(\sqrt{\max(q,3)},(-s)_+/4)=2.
\]

The torsion calculation survives with the same leading term:
\[
\boxed{\quad
t_\varepsilon(\exp_p(\varepsilon y))
=\rho_0(\bar z_1,\bar z_2)+O(\varepsilon)
\quad\text{in }C^1(\overline B_1).
\quad}                                                    \tag{7}
\]
The metric, spin connection and seed corrections only enter the remainder. The physical torsion is \(\varepsilon^{-1}\) times the torsion computed using \(g_\varepsilon\).

Consequently there is exactly one torsion zero near \(y=0\), at \(y=O(\varepsilon)\), with positive real index \(+1\). Choose
\[
m_*=\frac{128}{81},\qquad R_0=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3},
\]
so \(\rho_0^2R_0^2=m_*\). For a fixed cutoff \(\chi=1\) near zero and \(\chi=0\) above a threshold below \(m_*\), let \(B=B_g(p,R_0\varepsilon)\).

The established transgression \(dJ=c_2(E)\), \(E=S^-\otimes L\), gives exactly
\[
\int_Bc_2(E)-\int_{\partial B}J=1,
\qquad
\boxed{\quad
\int_Bd\chi\wedge J=1-\int_B\chi\,c_2(E).
\quad}                                                    \tag{8}
\]
The sign follows from the angular integral \(-1\) around the positive simple zero.

Physical determinant curvature is uniformly bounded. More precisely, the leading constant self-dual source gives
\[
F_A^-=O(\varepsilon),\qquad |F_A^+|^2=\frac89+O(\varepsilon^2).
\]
Because the background is hyperbolic, the supplied Chern density becomes
\[
16\pi^2c_2(E)
=\left[9(|F_A^+|^2-|F_A^-|^2)+\frac23\right]d\mu_g
=\left[\frac{26}{3}+O(\varepsilon^2)\right]d\mu_g.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\quad
\int_Bd\chi\wedge J=1+O(\varepsilon^4).
\quad}                                                    \tag{9}
\]
Its leading curvature density is \(13/(24\pi^2)\); the nonvanishing relative charge is carried predominantly by the boundary flux.

The critical radial concentration also persists unchanged. For fixed
\(0<a_0<b_0<m_*\) and \(T_\varepsilon=\{a_0<m_\varepsilon<b_0\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_{T_\varepsilon}|\nabla t|^4
&\longrightarrow8\pi^2(b_0^2-a_0^2),\\
\int_{T_\varepsilon}|\xi|^2|\nabla t|^2
&\longrightarrow\frac{8\pi^2}{3}(b_0^3-a_0^3),\\
\int_{T_\varepsilon}|dm|^2|\nabla t|^2
&\longrightarrow\frac{16\pi^2}{3}(b_0^3-a_0^3).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{10}
\]
The leading projected derivative \(N\) is zero; the actual \(N=O(1)\). Therefore
\[
\int_{T_\varepsilon}m|N|^2|\nabla t|^2=O(\varepsilon^2)\to0.
\]
The positive flux again survives in the radial torsion-length mode.

The ordinary local estimates are
\[
\rho=\rho_0+O(\varepsilon^2),\quad
\zeta=O(\varepsilon),\quad
\nabla\zeta=O(1),\quad P=O(1),
\]
\[
\int_B(|\nabla P|^2+|\nabla t|^2)=O(\varepsilon^2),\qquad
\int_B|F_A|^2=O(\varepsilon^4).
\]
Here the local geometric defect integral is identically zero. The other displayed quantities are integrated costs on the shrinking core, not averages normalized by core volume.

The boundary problem remains substantial. On \(\partial B\),
\[
m=m_*+O(\varepsilon),\qquad
\partial_\nu m=\frac{2\rho_0^2R_0}{\varepsilon}+O(1),
\]
and tangential torsion derivatives are \(O(\varepsilon^{-1})\). The unit torsion map has degree \(+1\), so it cannot join through a zero-free collar to a regular nonzero field extending over a ball with degree zero. Also \(F_A^-=O(\varepsilon)\) here, whereas the calibrated zero-end exterior has ASD determinant energy density approaching \(2/9\).

Thus the metric and canonical-weight mismatches of the flat model have been removed completely. Unfilled data remain the torsion winding and derivative matching, determinant-curvature matching, marked bundle identification, and the global fixed-class conformal-solvability condition. The local positive transition cost is compatible with the exact negative Einstein geometry and the exact weighted gauge equations; a global exclusion must use additional exterior or global compatibility.

## 395. 2026-09-27T03:16:57.420Z — zero_endpoint_system_20260927

Research thread: `01a0e086-9e15-7e60-8e58-fc4cb8d820b9`.

I41 gives a precise reduction of the coefficient problem, but its isotropic \(C_T(P+D)\) estimate cannot by itself yield coefficient \(4\). The following is suitable for a compact §3.2.

### Exact three-slack problem

Assume the actual all-metric family has
\[
p\ge A,\qquad a^2\ge T=A(1-h),\qquad
U=1+h+O(h^2),\qquad h\to0.
\]
Since the known upper bound tends to zero, I41 permits restricting the variational infimum to negative Yamabe representatives normalized by \(s=-4\).

For such a representative define
\[
x=\frac{P}{8\pi^2A},\quad
d=\frac{D}{36\pi^2A},\quad
\sigma=\frac{\Sigma}{32\pi^2A},\quad
z=\frac pA-1.
\]
All four quantities are nonnegative. Exact identities give
\[
\boxed{
e=1+h+2z+d,\qquad
\frac{V}{2\pi^2A}=1+z+\sigma,\qquad
x=h+z+d-\sigma,
}
\]
and therefore
\[
\boxed{\mathcal E=\mathcal J
=\frac{4(h+z+d-\sigma)}{1+h+2z+d}.}
\]
The opposite-chirality constraint becomes
\[
\boxed{d+2z\le4x+(U-1-h).}
\]

Thus the exact variational problem is the infimum of this displayed quotient over triples \((z,d,\sigma)\) **realized by actual normalized Yamabe metrics and their supplied classes**. It is not the infimum over arbitrary scalar triples satisfying these necessary inequalities.

### The real spinor remainder

For the same class, take an actual ordinary solution, with weight \(f=1\). This is a separately supplied solution; no estimate for the adapted variable-weight spinor is transferred to it.

Write
\[
\rho=|\Phi|^2,\quad K=\int|\nabla_A\Phi|^2,\quad
Q=\int(4-\rho)^2,\quad
J_+=\|F_A^+-(F_A^+)_H\|_2^2.
\]
The maximum principle gives \(0\le\rho\le4\). The actual equations yield
\[
4K=\int(4-\rho)\rho,\qquad
\int\rho^2=32\pi^2p+8J_+.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\boxed{\Sigma=8K+Q+8J_+,\qquad
\sigma=\frac{K+Q/8+J_+}{4\pi^2A}.}
\]
This identity holds for every such ordinary solution, so optimizing the choice of solution cannot change the combined remainder.

### The precise first-order target

Consider any actual candidate sequence with \(\mathcal E=O(h)\). The chiral upper bound and \(e\ge1+h+2z\) imply
\[
e=1+O(h),\qquad x,z,d,\sigma=O(h).
\]
Hence
\[
\frac{\mathcal E}{h}
=4-4\frac{\sigma-z-d}{h}+O(h).
\]

It follows that, along these sequences,
\[
\boxed{
\liminf\frac{\mathcal E}{h}\ge4
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{
\left[K+\frac18Q+J_+
-\frac19D-4\pi^2(p-A)\right]_+
}{Ah}\longrightarrow0.
}
\]

Equivalently, the needed first-order scalar-slack estimate is
\[
\Sigma\le\frac89D+32\pi^2(p-A)+o(Ah).
\]
This is an equivalent analytic target, not an estimate already proved by I41. It identifies the exact coefficient and the positive spinor losses that must be controlled. Merely bounding \(K\) is insufficient unless \(Q\) and \(J_+\) are also retained.

The stronger conditions \(\Sigma=o(Ah)\), or \(D=o(Ah)\) together with an appropriate rigidity estimate, would suffice but are not necessary. Sharp coefficient \(4\) only requires
\[
\sigma=z+d+o(h)
\]
on sharp minimizing sequences; it does not force the three slacks separately to vanish.

### Genuine cscK stress test

Take a product of closed hyperbolic surfaces and give the factors Gaussian curvatures
\[
-(1+t),\qquad -(1-t),\qquad 0<t<1.
\]
Put \(A_0=T=8(g_1-1)(g_2-1)\). These are genuine scalar-\(-4\), negative Yamabe, cscK metrics with actual canonical monopole input:
\[
p=\frac{A_0}{1-t^2},\qquad
P=\frac{8\pi^2A_0t^2}{1-t^2},\qquad
D=\Sigma=0.
\]
Their canonical ordinary spinor is parallel, with
\[
\rho=4,\qquad K=Q=J_+=0.
\]
Thus
\[
p-T=\frac{P}{8\pi^2}.
\]

Every universal estimate
\[
p-T\le C_T(P+D)
\]
must therefore have \(C_T\ge1/(8\pi^2)\), even arbitrarily close to KE. Accordingly I41’s
\[
c_0=(36\pi^2C_T)^{-1}
\]
satisfies \(c_0\le2/9\). Its displayed elimination bound (3.2), with \(U=1+h+O(h^2)\), certifies a slope \(18c_0/19\), at most \(4/19\). Improving this isotropic constant alone cannot establish \(4\).

This is a genuine test of the universal constant, not a counterexample in the tight small-\(h\) window: these products have \(h=0\) when \(A=A_0\). They are fully compatible with the proposed sharp spinor inequality, whose left side is zero.

### What happens to the known upper sequence

For each fixed surgery manifold, the classical shrinking-core sequence approaches the sharp absolute Ricci-energy bound. Its Yamabe representatives have no larger Ricci energy, while the same classical lower bound remains valid. Therefore their Ricci energies approach that same bound. The inherited energy-selection identities then give
\[
p\to A,\qquad D,\Sigma\to0,\qquad
\mathcal E\to\frac{4h}{1+h}.
\]
Choosing a sufficiently accurate diagonal sequence makes \(z,d,\sigma=o(h)\). Thus Yamabe normalization preserves—not improves—the known upper coefficient \(4\). The classical input is [LeBrun’s Theorem 4.3](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0003068).

The remaining improvement must therefore come from a sharper, anisotropic estimate on the actual spinor remainder above, not from scalar-variance removal alone. No files were edited.

## 397. 2026-09-27T03:54:53.196Z — sharp_cost_20260927b

Research thread: `01a0e0f2-f174-7d20-8bef-29d36e43e3c2`.

The strongest completed result is a sharper inverse-blowup criterion: only the caps’ self-dual Weyl energy matters. Neither scalar cap energy nor any modification of the handles is needed.

For
\[
M=X\#k\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\#\ell(S^1\times S^3),
\quad A=c_1^2(X),\quad h=(k+4\ell)/A,
\]
write \(S_0=32\pi^2A\), \(S=\int s^2\), \(L=\int(s-\bar s)^2\), \(R=\int|\operatorname{Ric}|^2\). Actual supply gives \(S\ge S_0\) and \(R\ge8\pi^2A(1+h)\).

Suppose actual smooth caps replace only the blowup cores, producing \(N=X\#\ell(S^1\times S^3)\), with the metrics agreeing on their full common exterior. Define
\[
C_+=\int_{\mathrm{caps}_N}|W^+|^2,\quad
K_+=\int_{\mathrm{cores}_M}|W^+|^2,\quad
B_N=\int_N|W^-|^2.
\]
Subtracting the two closed signature identities gives exactly
\[
B_M=12\pi^2k+B_N+K_+-C_+.
\]
Consequently,
\[
P_M=8\pi^2Ah+\frac{S-S_0}{12}+4(B_N+K_+-C_+),
\]
and, for \(0\le h\le1/3\),
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal E-\frac{4h}{1+h}
=
\frac{(1-3h)(S-S_0)/3+16(B_N+K_+-C_+)+(1+h)L}
{(1+h)R}.}
\]
Thus the finite, all-metric estimate is
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal E\ge\frac{4h}{1+h}
-\frac{16C_+}{(1+h)R}
\ge\frac{4h}{1+h}
-\frac{2C_+}{\pi^2A(1+h)^2}.}
\]

This requires no Yamabe replacement or tight chiral window. Actual compatible ASD caps give the finite sharp bound; \(C_+=o(Ah)\) gives coefficient \(4\). More generally, \(C_+\le K_+\) suffices for the finite sharp bound, allowing nonzero cap Weyl energy.

Conversely, every cap system satisfies
\[
16C_+\ge(1+h)R
\left(\frac{4h}{1+h}-\mathcal E\right)_+.
\]
Therefore a sequence with \(\mathcal E/h\to c<4\) forces
\[
\boxed{\liminf\frac{C_+}{Ah}\ge\frac{\pi^2}{2}(4-c).}
\]
The lower Ricci bound alone suffices here; \(e\to1\) is unnecessary.

Concrete sufficient cap hypotheses are \(\sum\operatorname{Vol}(C_i)\|W^+\|_{\infty,C_i}^2=o(Ah)\), or the existing Euclidean collar condition \(\sum\varepsilon_i^2=o(Ah)\). No scalar bound is required. Arbitrary boundary data are not asserted to admit cheap or ASD fillings.

The handle-only conclusion is also complete:
\[
\inf_g\mathcal E=\frac{4h}{1+h},
\qquad k=0,\quad0\le h\le1/3.
\]
Its lower bound follows from the exact identity above with no caps; the upper bound is the inherited [LeBrun construction](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0003068). For \(0<h<1/3\), scalar saturation would produce a nowhere-zero parallel positive spinor, contradicting \(c_2(S^+)=\ell>0\); hence the infimum is unattained. At \(h=1/3\), attainment remains undecided. Also \(\inf P=32\pi^2\ell\) for every \(\ell\).

I reviewed draft §§5–6: the existing formulas are correct. Section 6 should use this stronger Weyl-only replacement. Three exact identities were checked symbolically; the argument is an analytic deduction from classical identities, not a new gauge estimate. The balanced family’s unrestricted optimal coefficient remains unresolved. I made no file changes.

## 398. 2026-09-27T03:59:05.434Z — global_torsion_20260927b

Research thread: `01a0e0f3-4c4b-7641-a337-edcaf068d6dc`.

I obtained a complete conditional matching obstruction at the first-order ALE scale. It uses the full Einstein and positive-weight curvature equations, including their first-order connection source. It does not yet exclude an unrestricted endpoint sequence: the required first-order compactness and decay are stronger than the existing normalized budgets.

The bare signed-degree matching condition supplies no additional obstruction.

**1. Global degree matching is exactly the existing characteristic-number identity.**

For \(E_-=S^-\otimes L\), equation (7.1) gives
\[
c_2(E_-)[M]=\frac{9a^2+T_-}{4}.
\]
If \(t\) is zero-free outside disjoint balls containing only the constructed positive simple zeros, their number must therefore be
\[
N=\frac{9a^2+T_-}{4}.
\tag{A}
\]
The index of each core is exactly \(+1\); the \(O(\varepsilon^4)\) in its cutoff flux is the small curvature contribution, not uncertainty in its integer index.

At the endpoint,
\[
\frac NV
=\frac1{8\pi^2V}\int|W^-|^2+\frac5{12\pi^2}+o(1).
\tag{B}
\]
This has the correct positive sign for an all-positive collection.

Conversely, for a Hermitian rank-two bundle over a closed oriented four-manifold, condition (A) is sufficient for a *section-level* matching with those prescribed positive boundary germs. The unit-sphere fiber is \(S^3\), hence is \(2\)-connected. The only obstruction to extending the prescribed nonzero boundary sections across the exterior is the relative Euler class in degree four. Its evaluation is \(c_2(E_-)[M]-N\). There are no lower-dimensional obstructions or higher ones in dimension four. The extending section may be normalized to constant length on the exterior.

This is not a construction of the cubic torsion of a monopole. It establishes precisely that signed degree and clutching, without further differential information, cannot improve the already known Chern identity.

Nor does counting the explicit cores contradict the quadratic budgets. Their total local quadratic cost is \(O(N\varepsilon^2)\) and their total volume is \(O(N\varepsilon^4)\). Choosing
\[
N\varepsilon^2=o(V)
\]
makes both negligible, even if \(N/V\to\infty\). The exterior remains the substantive issue.

**2. A first-order ALE matching theorem.**

Let \((X,h)\) be a complete, one-ended hyperkähler ALE four-manifold, oriented so \(W_h^+=0\), with:

- nontrivial end group \(\Gamma\subset SU(2)_-\), acting freely on \(S^3\);
- the canonical spin structure, so \(S_h^+\) has a global parallel frame;
- \(H^1(X;\mathbb R)=0\).

These hypotheses include the usual simply connected Kronheimer ALE spaces. The finite-\(SU(2)\) ALE setting is also recorded in [Yan’s construction and classification discussion](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00208-024-02944-3). No assertion about extracting such a limit from the present endpoint sequence is included below.

Suppose, on an exhaustion of \(X\), an actual family has physical scale \(\varepsilon_j\to0\), rescaled metric \(h_j\), and
\[
\operatorname{Ric}(h_j)=-\varepsilon_j^2h_j,\qquad h_j\longrightarrow h
\]
smoothly on compact subsets. Its actual equations become
\[
D_{h_j,A_j}\Phi_j=0,\qquad
F_{A_j}^{+,h_j}
=i\varepsilon_j^2 f_j\,\sigma_{h_j}(\Phi_j).
\tag{C}
\]

Assume compatible unitary bundle identifications in which the **whole positive-spinor connection**, including Levi-Civita and determinant parts, and the spinor have first-order expansions
\[
\nabla_j^+=d+\varepsilon_j B+o(\varepsilon_j),\qquad
\Phi_j=\Phi_0+\varepsilon_j\psi+o(\varepsilon_j),
\tag{D}
\]
in \(C^1_{\rm loc}\) for the connection and \(C^2_{\rm loc}\) for the spinor. Here \(d\) is the parallel positive-spinor connection of \(h\), and \(\Phi_0\ne0\) is parallel.

Require
\[
\varepsilon_jf_j\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{locally},
\tag{E}
\]
and, for some \(\delta>0\),
\[
B=O(r^{-1-\delta}),\qquad dB=O(r^{-2-\delta}),
\qquad \psi=O(1+r).
\tag{F}
\]

Then the limiting physical covariant derivative vanishes:
\[
U:=d\psi+B\Phi_0=0.
\tag{G}
\]
Consequently the limiting physical cubic torsion vanishes:
\[
T=\sum_i c_h(e^i)\Phi_0\otimes(\Phi_0\wedge U_i)=0.
\tag{H}
\]
In particular this family cannot match a nonzero calibrated torsion field at this first-order ALE scale.

Here is a proof that retains, rather than suppresses, the first-order source.

Write \(B=\sum_{\alpha=0}^3 b_\alpha T_\alpha\) in a constant orthonormal basis of \(\mathfrak u(2)\), with \(T_0\) central. Since the background positive-spinor connection is flat, its first-order curvature is \(dB\).

For an Einstein metric the trace-free positive-spinor curvature is self-dual as a two-form: its anti-self-dual component is the trace-free Ricci block. Thus
\[
(db_\alpha)^-=0,\qquad \alpha=1,2,3.
\tag{I}
\]
Taking the first-order limit of the determinant equation in (C), using (E), gives
\[
(db_0)^+=0.
\tag{J}
\]
These statements do not require control of \(W^-\).

For a large ALE coordinate domain \(X_R\), Stokes gives
\[
\int_{X_R}|db_\alpha|^2
=\int_{\partial X_R}b_\alpha\wedge db_\alpha,
\qquad \alpha=1,2,3,
\]
and
\[
\int_{X_R}|db_0|^2
=-\int_{\partial X_R}b_0\wedge db_0.
\]
The boundary terms are \(O(R^{-2\delta})\), because the boundary area is \(O(R^3)\). Hence \(dB=0\).

Since \(H^1(X;\mathbb R)=0\), \(B=dG\) for a globally defined skew-Hermitian matrix \(G\). The decay in (F) implies that \(G\) tends to one constant matrix at infinity: radial integration gives a limit, while angular differences are \(O(r^{-\delta})\). Subtract that constant to arrange
\[
G=O(r^{-\delta}).
\]

The Dirac equation in (C) now has the exact first-order limit
\[
D_h\psi=-\sum_i c_h(e^i)B_i\Phi_0.
\tag{K}
\]
There is no omitted principal-symbol source: its variation multiplies \(d\Phi_0=0\). All first-order connection contributions are included in \(B\).

Set
\[
\psi'=\psi+G\Phi_0.
\]
Then
\[
D_h\psi'=0,\qquad U=d\psi',\qquad \psi'=O(1+r).
\tag{L}
\]

It remains to prove that this particular global harmonic spinor is parallel. Dirac zero alone is insufficient.

**ALE linear-growth lemma.** Every scalar harmonic function of at most linear growth on \(X\) is constant.

To prove it, lift the ALE end to \(\mathbb R^4\setminus B\), and for \(R\to\infty\) consider
\[
u_R(x)=\frac{u(Rx)-u(p)}{R}.
\]
The rescaled metrics tend smoothly to the Euclidean metric on every compact annulus. The linear growth bound and interior elliptic estimates yield subsequential smooth convergence on all such annuli to a \(\Gamma\)-invariant Euclidean harmonic function \(u_\infty\) satisfying
\[
|u_\infty(x)|\le C|x|.
\]
Its bounded singularity at the origin is removable. It is an entire harmonic function of linear growth, hence affine: applying the ordinary interior second-derivative estimate on arbitrarily large Euclidean balls gives \(D^2u_\infty=0\). Its value at the origin is zero, so it is linear.

A nontrivial element of \(\Gamma\) has no fixed vector, since its action on \(S^3\) is free. Therefore there is no nonzero \(\Gamma\)-invariant linear function. Thus \(u_\infty=0\).

The same argument for every subsequence, with \(C^1\) convergence on annuli, proves
\[
|\nabla u|\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{at infinity}.
\]
Bochner on the Ricci-flat metric gives
\[
\Delta_{\rm geom}|\nabla u|^2=2|\nabla^2u|^2\ge0.
\]
The nonnegative function \(|\nabla u|^2\) tends to zero at infinity, so the maximum principle makes it identically zero. This proves the lemma without assuming an asymptotic expansion for \(u\).

Finally, \(S_h^+\) has a global parallel frame, and the determinant background is flat. Lichnerowicz applied to (L) says that each component of \(\psi'\) is scalar harmonic. Each has at most linear growth, so the lemma makes every component constant. Hence \(U=d\psi'=0\), proving (G)–(H).

The end representation matters: \(S^+\) is trivial under \(\Gamma\), so its coefficients are invariant scalar functions. Allowing an unspecified nontrivial end representation would invalidate the linear-mode exclusion.

**3. Two useful refinements.**

First, condition (E) fits the actual canonical weight. For exact physical \(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\),
\[
f_0=\sqrt{4+\sqrt6|W_g^+|}.
\]
Because \(g_j=\varepsilon_j^2h_j\),
\[
\varepsilon_jf_0
=\sqrt{4\varepsilon_j^2+\sqrt6|W_{h_j}^+|}
\longrightarrow0
\]
locally as \(h_j\to h\) with \(W_h^+=0\). Smooth majorants chosen uniformly close to \(f_0\) retain this property. Thus bounded physical \(f_j\) is not needed.

Second, the growth assumption on \(\psi\) follows from natural matching bounds on the limiting torsion and current. Put \(\rho_0=|\Phi_0|^2\) and \(Z=\langle\Phi_0,U\rangle\). The linearized form of the exact Dirac decomposition (8.2) is
\[
0\le 2\rho_0^2|U|^2-|T|^2
\le4\rho_0|Z|^2.
\tag{M}
\]
Thus bounded \(T\) and \(Z\) on the ALE end imply bounded \(U\). Since \(B\) decays, \(d\psi=U-B\Phi_0\) is bounded, giving \(\psi=O(r)\). An exterior with
\[
|T|^2\to128/81,\qquad Z\to0
\]
therefore contradicts the theorem, provided it is an exterior of the **same global first-order limit**.

For the flat limit \(X=\mathbb R^4\), the corresponding argument makes \(\psi'\) affine, rather than constant. Then \(U\) and \(T\) are constant. A positive simple torsion zero cannot survive in such a bounded global limit. The existing quadratic core has \(T(y)\sim(\bar z_1,\bar z_2)\); its growth violates the bounded exterior condition, exactly as it should.

**4. What remains missing for the actual endpoint.**

This gives a concrete global matching alternative. A positive core cannot be extended through a complete hyperkähler ALE model with all of the following simultaneously: a first-order flat positive-spinor background, decaying first-order connection, bounded exterior torsion/current, and nonzero torsion persisting at that scale.

The present budgets do not force those conditions:

- Zeroth-order bubble convergence does not imply the \(O(\varepsilon_j)\) expansions in (D).
- Determinant-curvature saturation does not give the first-order decay in (F). Curvature of physical size \(O(\varepsilon^{-1})\) on an \(\varepsilon\)-ball costs only \(O(\varepsilon^2)\) in its \(L^2\) integral.
- Normalized convergence \(m\to128/81\) does not put nonzero torsion on a fixed compact subset of a shrinking bubble.
- Calibration can move to radii \(R_j\to\infty\) in bubble coordinates. Then the first-order limit may have \(T=0\) on every fixed compact set, while matching occurs at a later scale. The limits in \(j\) and radius cannot be interchanged.

The Stokes step identifies the corresponding spatial flux explicitly: a nonzero first-order connection source must retain boundary terms
\[
\int_{\partial X_R}
\left(\sum_{\alpha=1}^3b_\alpha\wedge db_\alpha
-b_0\wedge db_0\right)
\]
or violate the stated integrability/expansion hypotheses. It cannot be supplied by an isolated decaying first-order perturbation.

Thus this is a proved conditional obstruction to a proposed global matching mechanism, including its actual sourced correction equation. It is not a closed-manifold endpoint gap or a matched counterexample. No files were edited.

## 399. 2026-09-27T04:04:35.041Z — sharp_cost_20260927b

Research thread: `01a0e0f2-f174-7d20-8bef-29d36e43e3c2`.

The cap interface now has an exact filling theorem and an explicit obstruction.

Let a prescribed marked collar on \(B^4\) be conformal to the collar of a reference metric \(g_0\). Define
\[
b(g)=\int_{B^4}(|W_g^+|^2-|W_g^-|^2)
=4\pi^2\int_{B^4}p_1(\nabla^g).
\]
For two metrics agreeing on the full collar, identify their orthonormal frame bundles canonically. Their connection difference vanishes there, so relative Chern–Weil transgression gives equal \(b\). This comparison takes place on the same marked ball; it does not double inward collars.

Extend the prescribed positive conformal factor smoothly over \(B^4\). Conformal invariance of both Weyl integrals then gives:

\[
\boxed{
W^-_{g_0}=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\min_{\text{compatible caps}}\int|W^+|^2
=\int_{B^4}|W^+_{g_0}|^2.}
\]
Indeed every cap satisfies \(C_+=b(g_0)+C_-\), while the conformal extension of \(g_0\) attains equality.

For a complex-hyperbolic ball \(B_r\), normalized by \(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\),
\[
\boxed{\min C_+=\frac23\operatorname{Vol}_{CH}(B_r)>0.}
\]
Thus even arbitrarily thin prescribed CH collars forbid ASD or arbitrarily cheap caps at fixed radius. For several prescribed collars, the minimum is exactly \(\frac23\sum_i\operatorname{Vol}_{CH}(B_{r_i})\). Cheapness at scale \(Ah\) is equivalent to that sum being \(o(Ah)\).

Conversely, a collar conformal to a round Euclidean-ball collar has a compatible conformally flat cap with \(C_+=0\). Neither construction needs bounds on derivatives of the conformal factor. The transgression used here is classical; its source is [Chern–Simons, Characteristic Forms and Geometric Invariants](https://math.mit.edu/juvitop/pastseminars/notes_2019_Fall/Chern-Simons.pdf).

There is also a complete obstruction to using only the induced boundary conformal metric. On \(B^4\), choose
\[
d\sigma_i=-2\sigma_j\wedge\sigma_k,\qquad
\int_{S^3}\sigma_{123}=2\pi^2,
\]
and set
\[
g_t=dr^2+r^2(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)
+r^2F(r)^2\sigma_3^2,\qquad
F(r)=1+t r^2(1-r^2),\quad t>0.
\]
This is smooth at the center, and its induced boundary metric is the unit round metric for every \(t\).

Writing \(G=F+rF'\), its connection forms are
\[
\omega_{10}=\sigma_1,\quad \omega_{20}=\sigma_2,\quad
\omega_{30}=G\sigma_3,\quad
\omega_{12}=(F^2-2)\sigma_3,\quad
\omega_{13}=F\sigma_2,\quad
\omega_{23}=-F\sigma_1.
\]
Direct curvature calculation gives
\[
-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\Omega\wedge\Omega)
=
\frac{d}{dr}\left[-4(1-F^2)^2-2r^2(F')^2\right]
dr\wedge\sigma_{123}.
\]
Since \(F(0)=F(1)=1\) and \(F'(1)=-2t\),
\[
b(g_t)=-16\pi^2t^2.
\]
Pulling back by a reflection of \(B^4\) changes its sign while retaining the round induced boundary metric. Every cap matching this reflected full collar therefore satisfies
\[
\boxed{C_+\ge16\pi^2t^2.}
\]
Hence the same intrinsic round boundary metric is compatible with arbitrarily large compulsory cap cost. The missing information is in the extrinsic conformal germ. The full Cartan computation at \(t=1/4\) was independently integrated symbolically, yielding \(-\pi^2\).

I rechecked manuscript §§5–6: the all-metric quantifiers, signs and constants are correct. The only small clarification is to write \(0<h\to0\) in asymptotic ratio statements. These results do not establish that arbitrary low-defect metrics admit a favorable choice of exceptional cuts.

## 400. 2026-09-27T04:05:04.036Z — endpoint_geometry_20260927b

Research thread: `01a0e0f3-18be-7042-9a86-22dba44e3fe5`.

The verified extension is the global comparison-metric / fixed-scale nonconcentration theorem. The Euler-density-only extension remains conditional.

### 1. Comparison metric gives genuine covering noncollapse

**Proposition.** Fix \(a\ge1\), \(H<\infty\). There are \(\rho=\rho(a,H)>0\) and \(v=v(a)>0\) such that the following holds. Suppose \(M^4\) carries complete metrics \(g,h\) with
\[
a^{-1}h\le g\le ah,\qquad |\sec_h|\le H.
\]
For every \(x\), let
\[
\pi_x:(\widetilde{B^g_{4\rho}(x)},\tilde x)\longrightarrow B^g_{4\rho}(x)
\]
be its genuine universal cover, equipped with \(\pi_x^*g\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{\pi_x^*g}B_\rho(\tilde x)\ge v\rho^4.
\]

**Primary input.** CFG, *Nilpotent Structures and Invariant Metrics on Collapsed Manifolds*, JAMS 5 (1992): definition (1.1.4)–(1.1.5), printed p.331; Theorem 1.3, p.332. For a complete metric with \(|\sec|<1\), fixing their approximation parameter gives a uniformly equivalent \((\rho_0,k)\)-round metric with uniformly bounded curvature. At each center, the roundness supplies a **normal covering of an actual open neighborhood containing the \(\rho_0\)-ball**, with injectivity radius at the lifted center bounded below. The proof of the injectivity assertion is on p.365, ending with (8.9). [CFG primary PDF](https://www.ihes.fr/~gromov/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/384.pdf)

**Proof.** Set \(S=\max\{1,2H\}\). Apply CFG to \(Sh\), with approximation parameter \(\log2\), and rescale back. We obtain a metric \(k\) satisfying
\[
\tfrac12h\le k\le2h,\qquad |\sec_k|\le C_0S,
\]
and, for every \(x\), a genuine normal cover
\[
q:(N,\hat x)\longrightarrow(V,x),\qquad
B^k_s(x)\subset V,\quad s=\rho_0S^{-1/2},
\]
whose lifted \(k\)-metric has injectivity radius at \(\hat x\) at least \(s\).

Write \(A=2a\), so \(A^{-1}k\le g\le Ak\). Choose a dimensional \(d_0>0\) with
\[
d_0<\rho_0/2,\qquad \sqrt{C_0}\,d_0<1/2,
\]
and put
\[
\rho=\frac{d_0}{8\sqrt{AS}}.
\]
Then
\[
U:=B^g_{4\rho}(x)\subset B^k_{4\sqrt A\rho}(x)
\subset B^k_s(x)\subset V.
\]

Since \(\widetilde U\) is simply connected, the inclusion \(U\hookrightarrow V\) lifts to
\[
F:(\widetilde U,\tilde x)\longrightarrow(N,\hat x).
\]
This is a local isometry for the lifted **original metric \(g\)**.

Crucially,
\[
F(B_\rho^{\tilde g}(\tilde x))
\supset B_\rho^{q^*g}(\hat x).
\]
Indeed, take any path in \(N\) from \(\hat x\) of \(g\)-length \(<\rho\). Its projection stays in \(B^g_\rho(x)\subset U\), so it lifts to \(\widetilde U\). Uniqueness of path lifting makes its image under \(F\) the original path. No injectivity of \(F\), and no exponential-map covering assertion, is used.

These balls have the required completeness buffer. A finite-length path in a covering cannot escape over an interior limit point of its base: eventually it lies in one component above an evenly covered coordinate neighborhood. Thus the completion boundary above \(V\) is at \(k\)-distance at least \(s\) from \(\hat x\); similarly, the completion boundary of \(\widetilde U\) is at \(g\)-distance at least \(4\rho\) from \(\tilde x\).

Now
\[
B^k_{\rho/\sqrt A}(\hat x)\subset B^g_\rho(\hat x).
\]
The former lies below both the injectivity and curvature scales. Rauch comparison therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{k}B^k_{\rho/\sqrt A}(\hat x)
\ge c_4 A^{-2}\rho^4.
\]
Because \(dV_g\ge A^{-2}dV_k\), and the area formula applied to the surjective local isometry \(F\) gives a volume inequality,
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{\tilde g}B_\rho(\tilde x)
\ge c_4 A^{-4}\rho^4.
\]
Take \(v=c_4(2a)^{-4}\). ∎

Consequently, your established cover-coercivity/Liouville theorem gives
\[
\fint_M Z_t(g,\omega)\ge c(K,L,a,H)>0
\]
whenever additionally \(|\operatorname{Ric}_g|\le K\), \(|\omega|\le L\), and \(t\in[0,1/4]\). The supplied form never changes metric.

### 2. Li II supplies the comparison metric

For the unnormalized **full Riemann tensor** norm, Li’s arXiv Theorem 1.1 states that dimensional constants \(\varepsilon_4,c_4,C_4>0\) exist such that
\[
|\operatorname{Ric}_{g_0}|\le K,\qquad
\sup_x\int_{B_r(x)}|\operatorname{Rm}_{g_0}|^2\le\varepsilon_4,\quad r\le1,
\]
give a Ricci flow for a time at least
\[
c_4\min\{r^2,K^{-1}\},
\qquad |\operatorname{Rm}_{g(t)}|\le C_4/t.
\]
The quantitative statement is on preprint pp.4–5. The proof of Theorem 3.1, pp.13–15, includes the bootstrap condition (3.8) and its strict closure:
\[
\tfrac12g_0<g(t)<2g_0.
\]
Thus, after fixing a suitably small dimensional fraction of the guaranteed time,
\[
h=g(t_*),\qquad
\tfrac12g_0\le h\le2g_0,\qquad
|\sec_h|\le C\max\{r^{-2},K\}.
\]
[Li II full preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0911.3104)

**Closed-scope audit.** The arXiv v1 theorem literally says “complete noncompact”; the [published primary abstract](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10455-011-9290-0) explicitly states the compact result. The published PDF was not obtained. The closed application can also be justified directly by the same §3 bootstrap, using Hamilton’s closed initial existence and extension.

For this project there is a clean way to avoid the small-closed-manifold issue in the preprint’s pure Dirichlet Sobolev inequality. When \(\delta_\infty\le1/4\),
\[
\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|\operatorname{Ric}_0|^2}{2}\ge\frac14,
\]
so \(\chi(M)>0\), and
\[
\int_M|\operatorname{Rm}|^2\ge32\pi^2.
\]
Choose \(\varepsilon_4<32\pi^2\). The small-energy hypothesis then forces \(\operatorname{diam}M>r\). Perform the closed bootstrap at scale \(r/10\); every relevant ball has a uniform proper-ball buffer. This changes dimensional constants only. This should be recorded as the direct compact adaptation, not as a verbatim published theorem statement.

If the repository’s curvature-operator convention is used, \(|\operatorname{Rm}|^2=4|\mathcal R|^2\); replace the energy threshold by \(\varepsilon_4/4\).

### 3. Actual endpoint and upper-energy consequences

For each fixed \(r\in(0,1]\), the preceding results give
\[
\boxed{\quad
\delta_\infty^2+\frac{D_\beta}{V}\ge\varepsilon(r)>0
\qquad(\beta\ge4)
\quad}
\]
for the actual supplier, assuming \(\delta_\infty\le1/4\) and the uniform fixed-scale small-energy condition. Constants are independent of diameter, base-ball volume, Euler density, and any exact Einstein or critical-metric PDE.

Indeed, use the same supplied form with \(L=3\sqrt2\), \(t=1/\beta\), and
\[
\fint Z_t\le C\left(r_{\rm Ric}+D_\beta/V\right)+o(1),
\qquad r_{\rm Ric}\le4\delta_\infty^2,
\]
then send the selectable allowance to zero.

Under the existing §13 hypotheses \(p\ge A>0\), \(h\in[1/4,1/3]\), the already-proved algebra therefore gives
\[
\delta_\infty^2+(G(h)-e)_+
\ge
\min\left\{\frac1{64},\frac{\varepsilon(r)^2}{80000}\right\}.
\]
No additional class-square or Euler-density assumption is needed.

### 4. Supercritical curvature input

A concrete sufficient condition is, for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
\sup_{x\in M}\int_{B_1(x)}|\operatorname{Rm}|^{2+\eta}\le\Lambda.
\]
Bishop and Hölder give, for \(r\le1\),
\[
\int_{B_r(x)}|\operatorname{Rm}|^2
\le
\Lambda^{2/(2+\eta)}
\bigl(C(K)r^4\bigr)^{\eta/(2+\eta)}.
\]
Choose \(r=r(K,\eta,\Lambda)>0\) making this at most \(\varepsilon_4\). This yields the actual endpoint gap and upper-energy margin with constants depending only on \(K,\eta,\Lambda\). More generally, a uniform local \(L^2\)-equiintegrability modulus suffices.

### Remaining boundary

Li I’s full local theorem was not obtained through the bounded public author/publisher/repository search. Its abstract is encouraging, but it does **not** certify the precise uniform local smoothing hypothesis needed here. Nor should complete CFG Theorem 1.3 silently be substituted for its buffered local version.

Accordingly, keep
\[
|\operatorname{Ric}|\le K+\chi/V\text{ bounded}
\Longrightarrow\text{positive-fraction original covering noncollapse}
\]
conditional. The global comparison-metric and Li II routes above are the completed branch.

The mathematics Skill guided the separation of inherited coercivity, new covering arguments, and the remaining source-dependent claim. No files or live state were changed.

## 401. 2026-09-27T04:09:07.945Z — global_torsion_20260927b

Research thread: `01a0e0f3-4c4b-7641-a337-edcaf068d6dc`.

The pointwise decay assumption can be removed. On the stated ALE background, finite \(L^2\) energy of the first-order curvature already forces that curvature to vanish. The growth needed afterward should be imposed on the physical first derivative—or obtained from bounded torsion and current—not on the ungauged correction \(\psi\).

1. Strengthened ALE theorem

Retain the previous first-order family and actual equations:
\[
\operatorname{Ric}(h_j)=-\varepsilon_j^2h_j,\qquad
D_{h_j,A_j}\Phi_j=0,\qquad
F_{A_j}^{+,h_j}
=i\varepsilon_j^2 f_j\sigma_{h_j}(\Phi_j),
\]
with \(h_j\to h\) smoothly on compact subsets of a complete hyperkähler ALE four-manifold \(X\), oriented by \(W_h^+=0\). Assume its end group \(\Gamma\subset SU(2)_-\) is nontrivial and \(H^1(X;\mathbb R)=0\).

The background connection on the **full twisted positive-spinor bundle** must admit a global parallel unitary frame. Triviality of the untwisted \(S^+\), together with a merely flat determinant connection whose holonomy is unspecified, is not the stated hypothesis.

In that frame assume
\[
\nabla_j^+=d+\varepsilon_jB+o(\varepsilon_j),\qquad
\Phi_j=\Phi_0+\varepsilon_j\psi+o(\varepsilon_j),
\]
locally in the previously specified differentiability classes, with \(\Phi_0\ne0\) constant. Also assume \(\varepsilon_jf_j\to0\) locally. As previously checked, the canonical majorant satisfies this under \(h_j\to h\).

Replace all pointwise decay and ungauged growth assumptions by
\[
\int_X|dB|^2\,d\mu_h<\infty
\tag{1}
\]
and boundedness on the ALE end of
\[
U=d\psi+B\Phi_0.
\tag{2}
\]
Then \(U=0\), so the limiting physical torsion vanishes.

Boundedness of \(U\) can equivalently be supplied by bounded limiting torsion and current:
\[
T=\sum_i c_h(e^i)\Phi_0\otimes(\Phi_0\wedge U_i),
\qquad Z=\langle\Phi_0,U\rangle.
\]
Indeed the limiting exact Dirac algebra gives
\[
0\le2\rho_0^2|U|^2-|T|^2
\le4\rho_0|Z|^2,\qquad \rho_0=|\Phi_0|^2>0.
\tag{3}
\]

2. Eliminating the first-order curvature

Write
\[
B=\sum_{\alpha=0}^3 b_\alpha T_\alpha
\]
in a constant orthonormal basis of \(\mathfrak u(2)\), with \(T_0\) central and each \(b_\alpha\) real. The actual first-order equations give
\[
(db_\alpha)^-=0\quad(\alpha=1,2,3),\qquad
(db_0)^+=0.
\tag{4}
\]
The first relations follow from exact Einstein curvature. The last follows from the rescaled positive determinant-curvature equation.

Here is the required global lemma.

**Lemma.** If \(F=db\) is a smooth, globally exact, self-dual or anti-self-dual two-form on an ALE four-manifold with finite end group, and \(F\in L^2\), then \(F=0\).

The proof constructs an \(L^4\) primitive before integrating by parts; it does not assume the original primitive decays.

Lift \(b\) and \(F\) to the Euclidean end cover. Choose a radial cutoff \(\eta\) which vanishes inside a fixed ball and equals one outside a larger ball. Extend
\[
F_{\mathrm{ext}}=d(\eta b)
\]
by zero across the inner ball in \(\mathbb R^4\). This is a smooth closed two-form. It equals the lifted \(F\) outside a compact annulus, so
\[
F_{\mathrm{ext}}\in L^2(\mathbb R^4).
\]
The possibly large values of \(b\) on the fixed transition annulus cause no difficulty: that contribution is smooth and compactly supported.

On Euclidean space define the homogeneous Hodge potential
\[
\beta=d^*\Delta^{-1}F_{\mathrm{ext}}.
\]
Its Fourier multiplier gives
\[
d\beta=F_{\mathrm{ext}},\qquad
\|\nabla\beta\|_{L^2}\le C\|F_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_{L^2}.
\]
For completeness, closure gives \(\xi\wedge\widehat F=0\); hence
\[
\xi\wedge\iota_\xi\widehat F=|\xi|^2\widehat F,
\]
which proves the first identity at nonzero frequency. There is no \(L^2\) harmonic remainder on \(\mathbb R^4\). The homogeneous four-dimensional Sobolev inequality gives
\[
\beta\in L^4(\mathbb R^4).
\]
Local elliptic regularity makes \(\beta\) smooth. Averaging over the finite group \(\Gamma\), if necessary, preserves \(d\beta=F_{\mathrm{ext}}\) and the \(L^4\) bound, so \(\beta\) descends to the ALE end.

On that end,
\[
d(b-\beta)=0.
\]
Since
\[
H^1(S^3/\Gamma;\mathbb R)=0,
\]
there is a smooth function \(q\) with \(b-\beta=dq\). Extend \(q\), using a cutoff on a fixed annulus, to a smooth global function \(\widetilde q\) on \(X\). Then
\[
\widetilde b=b-d\widetilde q
\]
is a global primitive of \(F\) which equals \(\beta\) near infinity. Therefore
\[
\widetilde b\in L^4(X),\qquad d\widetilde b=F.
\tag{5}
\]

Let \(\chi_R\) be an ALE radial cutoff, one inside radius \(R\), zero outside \(2R\), with \(|d\chi_R|\le C/R\). If \(*F=\sigma F\), \(\sigma\in\{1,-1\}\), then
\[
\int_X\chi_R|F|^2
=-\sigma\int_Xd\chi_R\wedge\widetilde b\wedge F.
\]
Using Hölder with exponents \(4,2,4\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|\int d\chi_R\wedge\widetilde b\wedge F\right|
&\le\frac CR
  \operatorname{Vol}(A_R)^{1/4}
  \|\widetilde b\|_{L^4(A_R)}
  \|F\|_{L^2(A_R)}\\
&\le C
  \|\widetilde b\|_{L^4(A_R)}
  \|F\|_{L^2(A_R)}
\longrightarrow0,
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(\operatorname{Vol}(A_R)=O(R^4)\). Thus \(F=0\). This proves the lemma.

Apply it to every component in (4), using (1). It follows that
\[
dB=0.
\tag{6}
\]

3. Gauge and growth are separate steps

The global hypothesis \(H^1(X;\mathbb R)=0\) now gives \(B=dG\). No boundedness of \(G\) follows from finite curvature energy: once \(dB=0\), that energy says nothing about the size of a pure-gauge primitive.

The actual first-order Dirac equation is
\[
D_h\psi=-\sum_i c_h(e^i)B_i\Phi_0.
\]
Consequently
\[
\psi'=\psi+G\Phi_0,\qquad
D_h\psi'=0,\qquad d\psi'=U.
\tag{7}
\]
Bounded \(U\), either assumed or obtained from (3), implies
\[
|\psi'|\le C(1+r).
\]
This is the correct gauge-invariant way to obtain the growth hypothesis. Linear growth of \(\psi\) before removing \(B\) would not suffice without control of \(G\).

The ALE linear-growth lemma from the previous proof applies to the scalar components of \(\psi'\): the full positive background frame is parallel; Lichnerowicz makes its components harmonic; the blow-down has no \(\Gamma\)-invariant linear scalar modes. Thus every component is constant and \(U=0\).

This proves the stronger theorem. The former pointwise conditions
\[
B=O(r^{-1-\delta}),\qquad dB=O(r^{-2-\delta})
\]
are now only one sufficient route to finite curvature energy and controlled gauge growth.

4. Exact weakest flux condition

Define the first-order signed three-form
\[
\mathcal Q_B=
\sum_{\alpha=1}^3 b_\alpha\wedge db_\alpha
-b_0\wedge db_0.
\]
Using (4),
\[
d\mathcal Q_B=|dB|^2\,d\mu_h.
\tag{8}
\]

For nested compact domains \(X_R\),
\[
\int_{X_R}|dB|^2=\int_{\partial X_R}\mathcal Q_B.
\tag{9}
\]
Therefore it suffices that the signed boundary flux tend to zero along one exhausting sequence. In cutoff form, for \(0\le\chi_j\le1\) tending pointwise to one, the exact criterion is
\[
\liminf_j\left[-\int d\chi_j\wedge\mathcal Q_B\right]=0.
\tag{10}
\]
Fatou then forces \(dB=0\); conversely \(dB=0\) makes every such flux zero. No separate \(L^2\) hypothesis is needed if (10) is assumed directly.

These fluxes are invariant under \(B\mapsto B+dG\), because the change in \(\mathcal Q_B\) is exact. The lemma above shows that finite \(L^2(dB)\), exactness, the chiral equations and the ALE end topology automatically imply this flux condition after constructing a suitable primitive.

The remaining unproved input is still the first-order limit itself, its finite curvature energy, and bounded physical torsion/current at the matching scale. None follows merely from normalized endpoint convergence.

5. Cross-review of the new manuscript

Theorem 1’s polar integration and cover-to-base Liouville averaging are sound. The cut-time restriction is removed only after the valid radial Jacobian upper bound. The argument neither counts sheets nor applies comparison beyond a conjugate point. The \(4\rho\) covering domain provides the needed interior buffer.

Equations (5.2)–(5.5) and (6.2)–(6.7) check algebraically. In particular,
\[
B_M=12\pi^2k+B_N+K_+-C_+
\]
has the correct sign, its substitution cancels the blowup terms exactly, and the error coefficient in (6.3) follows from \(R_M\ge8\pi^2A(1+h)\). The handle nonattainment argument correctly uses scalar equality to obtain a parallel spinor and then contradicts \(c_2(S^+)=\ell>0\).

Three small fixes remain:

- Equation (5.2) contains a literal form-feed before `rac`; replace it with `\frac`.
- State explicitly “along \(h\to0\)” when concluding that \(C_+=o(Ah)\) implies \(\liminf\mathcal E/h\ge4\).
- Equation (1.7) asserts a measurable representative of \(w_\rho\) without proving measurability. The main theorem for measurable center sets is unaffected. A fully sufficient alternative is to state convergence of the upper integral: the continuous geodesic-average function in (1.5) gives a measurable majorant for every superlevel set \(\{w_\rho\ge v\}\), and the established outer-measure bound plus Bishop’s upper bound yields \(\fint^{*}w_\rho\to0\).

No files were edited.

## 402. 2026-09-27T04:11:45.621Z — global_torsion_20260927b

Research thread: `01a0e0f3-4c4b-7641-a337-edcaf068d6dc`.

Confirmed. Exact Einstein is unnecessary.

Under \(g_j=\varepsilon_j^2h_j\),
\[
\operatorname{Ric}(g_j)=\operatorname{Ric}(h_j),\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}(g_j)=\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}(h_j)
\]
as covariant tensors, while
\[
|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}(h_j)|_{h_j}
=\varepsilon_j^2|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}(g_j)|_{g_j}.
\]
Hence uniformly bounded physical Ricci gives
\[
\varepsilon_j^{-1}|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}(h_j)|_{h_j}
=O(\varepsilon_j)\to0.
\]

The precise local hypothesis
\[
\varepsilon_j^{-1}\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}(h_j)\to0
\]
is enough to make the first-order trace-free positive-spinor curvature self-dual:
\[
(dB_{\mathfrak{su}(2)})^-=0.
\]
Scalar curvature contributes to the self-dual block and need not be constant. The remaining proof is unchanged.

For the canonical majorant, the exact scaling is
\[
\varepsilon_j f_{0,j}
=\max\!\left\{
\sqrt{\max\!\left(-s_{h_j}+\sqrt6|W^+_{h_j}|,\,3\varepsilon_j^2\right)},
\frac{(-s_{h_j})_+}{4\varepsilon_j}
\right\}.
\]
Uniform physical Ricci implies \(s_{h_j}=O(\varepsilon_j^2)\); smooth convergence to the hyperkähler limit gives \(W^+_{h_j}\to0\). Thus \(\varepsilon_jf_{0,j}\to0\), including uniformly close smooth majorants.

With **only** trace-free Ricci \(o(\varepsilon_j)\), retain \(\varepsilon_j f_j\to0\) separately, or assume \((s_{h_j})_-=o(\varepsilon_j)\). Trace-free control alone does not directly control the majorant’s second branch.

The theorem therefore applies to actual approximate Einstein families satisfying these hypotheses, with its first-order expansion, finite curvature energy, and bounded limiting torsion/current conditions still explicit.

## 403. 2026-09-27T04:19:14.435Z — /root

Research thread: `01a05d0f-1ca1-7583-8bb1-5e6cd9855513`.

本轮已用三个干净上下文的 GPT‑6 Astra/max 子智能体持续并行，取得中间结论后又继续减弱假设、推导应用并检验反例。新增内容已经合入[同一份完整证明](/data/qiushi/research/Yau26_Research/continuation/20260927_covering_geometry_and_sharp_subfamilies.md)。

最重要的数学推进有三组。

1. **零端障碍覆盖了新的近 Einstein 输入。**  
   先证明：假想零端序列不仅底空间塌缩，其局部万有覆盖也必须在平均意义下塌缩。随后接通[已有平滑理论](https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.3104)，得到：固定尺度各球曲率 \(L^2\) 能量足够小时，
   \[
   \delta_-^2+\mathfrak D_\beta/V\ge c(r)>0,\qquad\beta\ge4.
   \]
   不要求直径、底空间非塌缩或精确 Einstein；统一局部 \(L^{2+\eta}\) 曲率预算也足够。

2. **锐利性得到真实子族上的精确答案，并继续推进到填充边界。**  
   对复双曲曲面只添柄的实际子族，证明了
   \[
   \inf_{\text{全部光滑度量}}\mathcal E=\frac{4h}{1+h},
   \qquad 0\le h\le\tfrac13.
   \]
   对一般吹起／添柄情形，进一步消去了逆手术帽的全部标量成本，只保留 \(W^+\) 能量。又算出了完整复双曲共形领口的精确最小填充代价，并构造反例说明：**内蕴边界同样是圆球，完整相容填充的代价仍可任意大。**缺失的信息确实在外在领口，而不只是边界拓扑。

3. **实际集中核心获得了全局匹配障碍。**  
   在正文明确的一阶 ALE 极限条件下，有限一阶曲率能量与有界物理导数迫使极限扭率为零，不能匹配非零校准外部。继续推导后，已去掉最初的联络逐点衰减要求，也去掉了精确 Einstein 要求。但一阶紧性和同尺度匹配条件尚未由原始平均预算推出。

这三组工作的共同中心仍然清楚：**实际规范场怎样限制退化几何，以及拓扑代价究竟由哪些曲率与匹配信息支付。**

平衡吹起族的最优系数、无附加几何条件的零端间隙仍未解决，不能把上述受限结论扩大成它们的答案。

当前入口、结果目录和修订记录均已同步；按项目数学 Skill 保留了实际类、权重和局部／全局量词。40 项有限代数检查通过，证明审读另行记录。已本地提交 `cee6c6b`，没有制作新网页上传包，也没有外传。

## 404. 2026-09-27T08:08:32.573Z — multiscale_matching_20260927c

Research thread: `01a0e1dd-8121-70a1-9c7c-32f7b0abeb63`.

A new annular obstruction gives an actual multiscale alternative without the first-order hypotheses of §7. The following is manuscript-ready, subject to your review. No files were changed.

Let the actual supplied solution satisfy the hypotheses of the zero-end system, including \(a^2\ge T_+\), \(\beta\ge4\), and
\[
\eta=\kappa+\varepsilon_{\rm aux}\le1,
\qquad
\kappa=\fint|\operatorname{Ric}+g|^2+D_\beta/V.
\]
Retain
\[
P=\nabla_A\Phi,\quad \rho=|\Phi|^2,\quad
t=t_\Phi\in E_-=S^-\otimes L,\quad m=|t|^2,
\]
and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_\beta&=\frac{2\sqrt{4(1+\beta^{-1})}}3,\\
U_\beta&=\frac43(2\beta^{-1}-1),\\
m_\beta&=-\frac12U_\beta\rho_\beta^3,\\
S&=m_\beta+2\rho^2|P|^2,\qquad
d=2\rho^2|P|^2-m\ge0,\\
J&=\frac{(S-2m_\beta)^2}{S},\qquad
\mathcal A=(\rho-\rho_\beta)^2+J+d,\\
\mathcal R&=D^-_{3A}t.
\end{aligned}
\]

The inherited estimates give
\[
\boxed{
\int_M\mathcal A\le C\sqrt\eta\,V,\qquad
\int_M|\mathcal R|^{4/3}\le C\eta^{2/3}V.
}
\tag{A}
\]
Indeed \(J\) is controlled by the reciprocal test, \(d\le4\rho|\zeta|^2\), and the actual prolonged Dirac equation gives
\(\|\mathcal R\|_{4/3,\mathrm{avg}}\le C\sqrt\eta\).

For every measurable \(B\subset M\),
\[
\boxed{
\int_B|F_A|^2\le C\operatorname{Vol}(B)
 +C(\beta^{-1}+\sqrt\eta)V.
}
\tag{B}
\]
The negative-chiral part is precisely determinant-curvature saturation. For the positive part, use
\[
|F_A^+|^2=\frac18 f^2\rho^2,\qquad \rho\le4,
\qquad \int_M(f-\sqrt{4(1+\beta^{-1})})^2\le C\eta V.
\]
Thus (B) is a localized estimate for the full determinant curvature.

**Theorem — annular alternative at an arbitrary physical scale.**
Fix a nontrivial finite subgroup
\(\Gamma\subset SU(2)_-\), acting freely on \(S^3\), and put
\[
Q_\Gamma=\{1/2<|y|<4\}/\Gamma
\]
with its flat cone metric \(h_C\). There exist \(c_\Gamma,\delta_\Gamma>0\) such that the following holds.

Suppose \(\iota:Q_\Gamma\to M\) is an embedded annulus and \(r>0\) satisfies
\[
\|r^{-2}\iota^*g-h_C\|_{C^2(Q_\Gamma)}<\delta_\Gamma.
\]
Then the actual fields satisfy
\[
\boxed{
c_\Gamma\le
r^{-4}\int_{\iota(Q_\Gamma)}\mathcal A
+\int_{\iota(Q_\Gamma)}|F_A|^2
+r^{-8/3}\int_{\iota(Q_\Gamma)}|\mathcal R|^{4/3}.
}
\tag{C}
\]
The constants can be chosen uniformly when \(\Gamma\) ranges over a fixed finite family of nontrivial groups. Uniformity over arbitrary groups is not asserted.

There is no first-order expansion, finite first-order curvature-energy assumption, prescribed determinant character, or relation between \(r\) and an ALE core scale.

**Proof.**
Suppose instead that the rescaled metrics converge to \(h_C\) and all three terms on the right tend to zero. Transport the physical fields under the homothetic bundle identification. In particular, transport \(t\) without changing its amplitude. The rescaled field is
\[
\widetilde t=r^{-1}t_{\Phi,h},
\]
where \(t_{\Phi,h}\) denotes the cubic torsion recomputed with the rescaled metric. Likewise, \(S,J,d\) are transported physical scalars; they are not recomputed using the rescaled gradient.

The equations and norms transform as
\[
D^+_{h,A}\Phi=0,\qquad
D^-_{h,3A}\widetilde t=r\,\mathcal R,
\]
\[
\int_{Q_\Gamma}|F_A|_h^2
=\int_{\iota(Q_\Gamma)}|F_A|_g^2,
\qquad
\int_{Q_\Gamma}|D^-_{h,3A}\widetilde t|^{4/3}
=r^{-8/3}\int_{\iota(Q_\Gamma)}|\mathcal R|^{4/3}.
\tag{D}
\]

Use the canonical spin lift \(\gamma\mapsto(1,\gamma)\).
Every Spin-c structure on this annulus has the form
\[
S^\pm=\Sigma^\pm\otimes K,\qquad
L=K^2,\qquad
E_-=\Sigma^-\otimes K^3.
\tag{E}
\]
Because \(H^2(Q_\Gamma;\mathbb R)=0\), the line bundle \(K\) is torsion and admits a flat connection. Its flat characters form a finite set, so pass to a subsequence with a fixed character \(\chi:\Gamma\to U(1)\).

Relative to this flat connection, the connection on \(K\) differs by a global imaginary one-form. Since \(H^1(Q_\Gamma;\mathbb R)=0\), the Neumann Coulomb gauge and the ordinary Hodge estimate give
\[
\|a_j\|_{W^{1,2}(Q_\Gamma)}
\le C\|da_j\|_2
=\frac C2\|F_{A_j}\|_2\longrightarrow0.
\tag{F}
\]
This is an abelian estimate on one fixed annulus; no global Sobolev assumption on the degenerating closed manifold is used. In particular \(a_j\to0\) in \(L^4\).

After passing to another subsequence, \(\beta_j\) has a limit in \([4,\infty]\); both limiting reference masses remain strictly positive. The vanishing \(\mathcal A\)-integral gives
\[
|\Phi_j|^2\longrightarrow\rho_\infty
\quad\text{in }L^2.
\]
For the torsion, the useful elementary identities are
\[
J_j=S_j-4m_{\beta_j}+\frac{4m_{\beta_j}^2}{S_j}
\ge S_j-4m_{\beta_j},
\]
\[
\int|S_j-2m_{\beta_j}|
\le\left(\int J_j\right)^{1/2}
   \left(\int S_j\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Thus \(\int S_j\) is bounded and
\[
m_j=S_j-m_{\beta_j}-d_j
\longrightarrow m_\infty
\quad\text{strongly in }L^1.
\tag{G}
\]
Consequently the functions \(|\widetilde t_j|^2\) are uniformly integrable.

On smaller annuli containing \(\{1<|y|<2\}/\Gamma\), the positive Dirac equation, \(|\Phi_j|\le2\), and (F) give a uniform \(W^{1,2}\) bound for \(\Phi_j\). For the negative field, the interior first-order estimate gives
\[
\|\widetilde t_j\|_{W^{1,4/3}(Q')}
\le C\left(
\|D^-_{h_j,3A_j}\widetilde t_j\|_{4/3}
+\|a_j\widetilde t_j\|_{4/3}
+\|\widetilde t_j\|_{4/3}\right)\le C,
\]
using
\(\|a_j\widetilde t_j\|_{4/3}
\le\|a_j\|_4\|\widetilde t_j\|_2\).

The embedding \(W^{1,4/3}\to L^2\) is critical and is **not** invoked as compact. Rellich supplies convergence in \(L^q\), \(q<2\), and almost everywhere. Equation (G) supplies uniform integrability of the squared norms, so Vitali upgrades this to strong \(L^2\) convergence. Both limiting spinors therefore solve the flat twisted Dirac equations and have positive constant length. Elliptic regularity and the flat Lichnerowicz identity make both parallel.

The positive representation in (E) has holonomy \(\chi(\gamma)I\). Its nonzero parallel spinor forces \(\chi=1\). The negative bundle then has holonomy \(\gamma\), because its character is \(\chi^3\). A nonidentity element of \(SU(2)\) has no eigenvalue \(1\); hence this bundle has no nonzero parallel section. Contradiction. This also resolves all possible square-root and spin-structure twists: they are included in \(K\). ∎

**Corollary — packing at unrelated scales.**
Let \(A_i=\iota_i(Q_{\Gamma_i})\) satisfy (C), with multiplicity at most \(\Lambda\), groups in a fixed finite family, and radii \(r_i\le r_{\max}\). For sufficiently small \(r_{\max}\), depending only on the fixed annular constants and \(\Lambda\),
\[
\boxed{
\frac{\sum_i r_i^4}{V}
\le C_\Lambda\left[
\sqrt\eta
+r_{\max}^4(\beta^{-1}+\sqrt\eta)
+r_{\max}^{4/3}\eta^{2/3}
\right].
}
\tag{H}
\]

Indeed multiply (C) by \(r_i^4\), sum, and use (A). If \(U=\bigcup_iA_i\), the curvature term is bounded by
\[
\sum_i r_i^4\int_{A_i}|F_A|^2
\le \Lambda r_{\max}^4
 \left(C\operatorname{Vol}(U)
       +C(\beta^{-1}+\sqrt\eta)V\right).
\]
The annular geometry gives
\(\operatorname{Vol}(U)\le C\sum_i r_i^4\).
Its contribution is absorbed for small \(r_{\max}\), proving (H).

Suppose additionally that every annulus is calibrated in the precise sense
\[
r_i^{-4}\int_{A_i}\mathcal A\le c/2,
\]
where \(c\) is a common constant in (C). Then
\[
\boxed{
\frac{\sum_i r_i^{8/3}}V
\le C_\Lambda\left[
\eta^{2/3}
+r_{\max}^{8/3}(\beta^{-1}+\sqrt\eta)
\right].
}
\tag{I}
\]
No individual determinant-curvature hypothesis is needed. Subtract the calibration term from (C), multiply by \(r_i^{8/3}\), and use (B). The volume contribution is absorbed using
\[
\sum_i r_i^4\le
r_{\max}^{4/3}\sum_i r_i^{8/3}.
\]

For a zero-end sequence, suppose there are \(N_j\ge\nu V_j\) such annuli with comparable radii
\[
r_j\le r_{i,j}\le C_0r_j.
\]
As \(\beta_j\to\infty\) and \(\eta_j\to0\), (H) implies
\[
\boxed{r_j=O_{\nu,C_0,\Lambda}(\eta_j^{1/8}).}
\tag{J}
\]
To see this, absorb the term proportional to
\(r_j^4(\beta_j^{-1}+\sqrt{\eta_j})\), then apply Young to
\(r_j^{4/3}\eta_j^{2/3}\). This gives
\(r_j^4\le C_\nu(\sqrt{\eta_j}+\eta_j)\).

If these annuli are calibrated, (I) instead gives
\[
\boxed{r_j=O_{\nu,C_0,\Lambda}(\eta_j^{1/4}).}
\tag{K}
\]
Thus an escape radius \(R_j=r_j/\epsilon_j\to\infty\) is constrained by actual budgets even though no relation between \(\epsilon_j\) and \(\eta_j\) was assumed. It remains possible when the core scale is sufficiently smaller than the permitted physical matching scale.

The exact remaining bridge is geometric. Positive signed \(c_2(E_-)\) charge does not force nontrivial quotient necks: the existing actual positive-index cores on a fixed hyperbolic ball have trivial-group flat tangent annuli. Even when all zeros are positive and simple, the resulting lower bound for their number does not provide a positive density of nontrivial conical annuli, controlled overlap, or calibrated matching annuli. Nor do the present weak budgets ensure that a conical approximation persists out to an escaping radius. Accordingly, (C)–(K) advance the multiscale matching problem but do not prove the unrestricted zero-end gap.

- [Actual Dirac residual, §2](/data/qiushi/research/Yau26_Research/continuation/20260927_mixed_current_and_signed_cores.md:134), especially (2.2)–(2.3).
- [Actual Jensen defect and \(d\), §8](/data/qiushi/research/Yau26_Research/continuation/20260927_mixed_current_and_signed_cores.md:767), especially (8.1)–(8.4).
- [Determinant saturation, §6](/data/qiushi/research/Yau26_Research/continuation/20260927_conformal_separation_and_zero_end.md:532), especially (6.2)–(6.4).
