## 405. 2026-09-27T08:15:30.389Z — local_smoothing_euler_20260927c

Research thread: `01a0e1dd-19b8-7312-bd57-3e583e0d63ad`.

The general bounded-Ricci, normalized-Euler-density endpoint gap does follow. The missing classical input is explicitly stated in Cheeger–Tian, Theorem 0.8 together with Remark 8.22—not merely in Li I’s abstract.

## 1. Audited classical input

For fixed \(K\), sufficiently small **unnormalized**
\[
\int_{B_r(x)}|R_{\rm op}|^2\le \varepsilon_{\rm CT}(K),\qquad r\le1,\quad |\mathrm{Ric}|\le K,
\]
gives uniformly controlled local covering geometry on an interior ball, in \(C^{1,\alpha}\) and \(W^{2,q}\), for fixed \(\alpha<1,\ q<\infty\). This conclusion does **not** give a pointwise curvature bound for arbitrary bounded-Ricci metrics.

Source: [Cheeger–Tian, *Curvature and injectivity radius estimates for Einstein 4-manifolds*](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/Courses/MAT683/201001/MAT683S10.pdf), printed pp.489 and 515. The source explains covering geometry using genuine local universal covers and harmonic coordinates in Remarks 2.7 and 4.8, printed pp.501 and 507. Its bounded-Ricci extension is independently used in [Lott, §3.1](https://math.berkeley.edu/~lott/4d3.pdf).

The course PDF page number equals printed page minus 46. No downloaded files were retained. A reproducible read-only command is:
```bash
curl -L --max-time 55 --silent --show-error \
  'https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/Courses/MAT683/201001/MAT683S10.pdf' |
  pdftotext -f 469 -l 469 -layout - -
```

Use Remark 4.8 to interpret covering geometry, **not** as an isolated fixed-scale theorem without an energy hypothesis.

After applying the local theorem to \(r^{-2}g\), the Ricci bound is \(Kr^2\le K\). Consequently, at each good center there are uniform \(a,Q>0\), depending only on \(K\), and a smooth local diffeomorphism
\[
F_x:B_{\mathbb R^4}(0,ar)\longrightarrow M,\qquad F_x(0)=x,
\]
obtained by composing an unwrapped harmonic chart with its covering projection, such that
\[
Q^{-1}g_{\rm Euc}\le F_x^*g\le Qg_{\rm Euc}.
\]
No volume lower bound downstairs is required.

## 2. Precise local-isometry extension of I43

Theorem 1 remains valid if, at every \(x\in G\), a genuine universal cover is replaced by any pointed local isometry
\[
F_x:(N_x,\gamma_x,z_x)\to(M,g,x)
\]
such that \(\overline{B_{4\rho}^{\gamma_x}(z_x)}\) is compactly contained in \(N_x\) and
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{\gamma_x}B_\rho(z_x)\ge v\rho^4.
\]

Indeed, pull back \(g,\omega\), and \(Z_t\). The inherited buffered local coercivity gives
\[
\int_{B_{2\rho}^{\gamma_x}(z_x)}F_x^*Z_t\ge\epsilon(K,L,\rho,v).
\]
Polar integration before the cut time and Bishop’s radial Jacobian bound give
\[
\epsilon\le C_J(K,\rho)\int_{S_xM}\int_0^{2\rho}
s^3Z_t(\exp_x^g(s\theta))\,ds\,d\theta.
\]
This works because a \(\gamma_x\)-geodesic projects to a geodesic of the **original \(g\)**. Drop the cut restriction only after the Jacobian estimate.

Integrating this pointwise inequality over \(G\), enlarging to all centers, and applying invariance of the original \(g\)-Liouville measure yields
\[
\epsilon\operatorname{Vol}(G)
\le C_J(K,\rho)|S^3|\frac{(2\rho)^4}{4}\int_M Z_t.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Vol}(G)}V\le C(K,L,\rho,v)\fint_M Z_t.
\]

There is no sheet counting, no measurable-family-of-charts requirement, and no use of a geodesic flow belonging to a smoothed metric.

For the charts supplied above, set
\[
\rho=\frac{ar}{8\sqrt Q},\qquad \gamma_x=F_x^*g.
\]
Uniform ellipticity gives
\[
B_{4\rho}^{\gamma_x}(0)\subset B_{\rm Euc}(0,ar/2),\qquad
\operatorname{Vol}_{\gamma_x}B_\rho(0)\ge\omega_4Q^{-4}\rho^4.
\]
Hence they meet exactly these buffered hypotheses.

## 3. General Euler-density theorem

**Theorem.** Given \(K,L,\Lambda_0\), there is \(c(K,L,\Lambda_0)>0\) such that every closed oriented four-manifold satisfying
\[
|\mathrm{Ric}|\le K,\qquad
\frac{8\pi^2\chi(M)}V\le\Lambda_0
\]
and every smooth self-dual \(\omega\), \(|\omega|\le L\), satisfy
\[
\boxed{\ \fint_M Z_t\ge c(K,L,\Lambda_0),\qquad 0\le t\le\tfrac14.\ }
\]

**Proof.** In the manuscript’s curvature-operator convention,
\[
\int_M|R_{\rm op}|^2=8\pi^2\chi(M)+\int_M|\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\fint_M|R_{\rm op}|^2\le E_*,
\qquad E_*=1+K^2+\max\{\Lambda_0,0\}.
\]
Bishop comparison supplies
\[
\operatorname{Vol}B_r(y)\le C_B(K)r^4,\qquad r\le1.
\]
For \(A_r(x)=\int_{B_r(x)}|R_{\rm op}|^2\), Fubini gives
\[
\fint_M A_r(x)\,d\mu(x)\le C_B(K)r^4E_*.
\]
Choose
\[
r=\min\left\{1,
\left[\frac{\varepsilon_{\rm CT}(K)}{2C_B(K)E_*}\right]^{1/4}\right\}.
\]
Then the measurable set
\[
G=\{x:A_r(x)\le\varepsilon_{\rm CT}(K)\}
\]
has volume at least \(V/2\). Cheeger–Tian supplies the preceding uniformly buffered charts at every such center. Section 2 therefore gives the asserted gap. ∎

Changing to the four-index curvature norm changes the energy threshold by the corresponding factor \(4\); it does not change the argument.

Only one fixed finite \(q>4\) is needed. Alternatively, local coercivity can be proved directly on these \(W^{2,q}\) charts: metric compactness, local Hodge estimates for the self-dual forms, and their amplitude bound produce the forbidden smooth negative-Einstein limiting model. This bypasses a separate Cheeger–Naber regular-chart extraction.

## 4. Actual-input and upper-wall conclusions

Composing with the existing **same-form** actual supplier, preserving its fixed-class-through-auxiliary-weights requirement, gives
\[
\boxed{\ r_{\rm Ric}+\frac{D_\beta}{V}
       \ge c(K,\Lambda_0)>0,\qquad\beta\ge4.\ }
\]
The freely selectable supplier error is sent to zero after applying the geometric estimate.

For \(\delta_-=\|\mathrm{Ric}^{\sharp}+I\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}\le1/4\), the Ricci bound is uniform and \(r_{\rm Ric}\le4\delta_-^2\), so
\[
\delta_-^2+D_\beta/V\ge c(\Lambda_0)>0.
\]
The unchanged I43 §3 algebra then yields, with its existing actual hypotheses \(p\ge A>0\), \(T_+=A(1-h)\), and \(h\in[1/4,1/3]\),
\[
\boxed{\ \delta_-^2+(G(h)-e)_+\ge c'(\Lambda_0)>0.\ }
\]
Thus the elliptic-metric restriction in I43 §4 can be removed. Neither diameter nor an auxiliary Hessian budget is needed.

## 5. The \(\chi/A\) application

Assume \(p\ge A>0\), \(\chi(M)/A\le B\), and bounded Ricci. For \(r=r_{\rm Ric}\le1\),
\[
\fint s^2\le(4+2\sqrt r)^2,\qquad
\int s^2\ge32\pi^2A.
\]
Hence
\[
V\ge\frac{32\pi^2A}{(4+2\sqrt r)^2},
\qquad
\frac{8\pi^2\chi(M)}V\le9\max\{B,0\}.
\]
The new theorem supplies \(r+D_\beta/V\ge c(K,B)>0\). For \(r>1\), the same conclusion follows from \(D_\beta\ge0\), after decreasing the constant. The pointwise near-Einstein version consequently has a constant depending only on \(B\), and gives the corresponding diameter-free upper-wall margin.

Finally, any bounded-Ricci/amplitude sequence with \(\fint Z_{t_j}\to0\)—or corresponding actual zero-end sequence—must satisfy
\[
\boxed{\ \frac{8\pi^2\chi(M_j)}{V_j}\longrightarrow+\infty.\ }
\]
This is divergence, not merely subsequential unboundedness.

The unrestricted weak-\(L^2\) problem **without** a uniform Ricci bound remains open. Constants here are non-effective because the inherited local coercivity is compactness-based.

I used the project mathematics skill to keep the verified classical input, the new deduction, and the remaining analytic limitation separate. No files or live state were changed.

## 406. 2026-09-27T08:15:56.846Z — balanced_coefficient_20260927c

Research thread: `01a0e1dd-4ec5-7220-a95a-89911e5125c1`.

The all-metric coefficient remains open. A new sufficient condition can be stated in terms of nonintegrability energy, and it survives isolated spinor zeros.

For a scalar \(-4\) metric with the actual budget \(V\ge2\pi^2A\), let \(\omega\in W^{1,2}(\Lambda^+)\) satisfy \(|\omega|^2=2\) almost everywhere. Define
\[
d\omega=\theta\wedge\omega,\qquad
\Theta=\int|\theta|^2,\qquad
\nu=\int\bigl(|\nabla\omega|^2-|\theta|^2\bigr),\qquad
t=\nu-\Theta.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{P\ge8\pi^2Ah+4(V-2\pi^2A)-2\nu+2\Theta+
\frac{3(\nu-\Theta)^2}{8V}.}
\]

Indeed, integrated Weitzenböck gives
\[
\int\langle W^+\omega,\omega\rangle=\frac t2-\frac{4V}{3}.
\]
Tracefree Cauchy–Schwarz consequently gives
\[
\int|W^+|^2\ge\frac{2V}{3}-\frac t2+\frac{3t^2}{32V}.
\]
Substitution into positive Chern–Weil proves the claim.

The pointwise quantity defining \(\nu\) is nonnegative. In a quaternionic frame,
\(\nabla\omega=a\otimes\omega_2+b\otimes\omega_3\), it is
\[
|*(a\wedge\omega_2)-*(b\wedge\omega_3)|^2.
\]
For a smooth compatible almost-complex structure,
\[
\nu=\frac18\int|N_J|^2
\]
when the Nijenhuis norm sums over all ordered index pairs. I checked this coefficient symbolically. The usual Hermitian curvature identities provide an independent normalization check. [Apostolov–Muškarov, equations (9)–(10)](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/article/AIF_1999__49_5_1673_0.pdf).

Using the inherited \(R\ge8\pi^2A(1+h)\), for \(0\le h\le1/3\),
\[
\boxed{\mathcal E\ge\frac{4h}{1+h}
-\frac{(\nu-\Theta)_+}{\pi^2A(1+h)^2}.}
\]
Therefore \((\nu-\Theta)_+=o(Ah)\) suffices for coefficient \(4\). The stronger condition \(\nu=o(Ah)\) has a direct nonintegrability interpretation. Conversely, if \(\mathcal E/h\to c<4\), every such weak unit form satisfies
\[
\liminf\frac{(\nu-\Theta)_+}{Ah}\ge\pi^2(4-c).
\]

For smooth Hermitian metrics, \(\nu=0\). Conformal Yamabe reduction preserves Hermitian compatibility, so the exact bound \(4h/(1+h)\) holds for every Hermitian metric in the stated actual-supply setting. This does not assert that the balanced manifolds admit Hermitian structures.

The weak formulation matters: a smooth spinor with finitely many transverse zeros yields a normalized projective form with \(|\nabla\omega|=O(r^{-1})\), hence finite \(W^{1,2}\) energy in dimension four. Points have zero \(W^{1,2}\) capacity, so the proof extends across them. No smooth global almost-complex structure is required. General actual zero sets and the required small torsion energy remain uncontrolled.

A completely smooth alternative also retains zeros. For any nonzero smooth self-dual \(\omega_0\), put
\[
a=\tfrac12\int|\omega_0|^2,\quad b=\tfrac14\int|\omega_0|^4,\quad
V_{\rm eff}=a^2/b,\quad T_0=\int(|\nabla\omega_0|^2-2|d\omega_0|^2).
\]
The same argument gives
\[
P\ge8\pi^2Ah+4(V-2\pi^2A)
-\frac83(V-V_{\rm eff})-2(a/b)T_0+\frac{3T_0^2}{8b}.
\]
For the ordinary actual form \(\omega_0=iF_A^+\),
\[
V-V_{\rm eff}\le K/2+Q/16.
\]
Existing estimates give only \(O(Ah)\), not \(o(Ah)\); this does not close the coefficient.

Other checks:

- The standard pencil gives
  \[
  S_2/3+16W_+=(8/27)D_8+(64/3)\pi^2p.
  \]
  Thus \(D_8\ge0\) supplies only two-thirds of the requested bound at \(p=A\). At CH calibration \(D_8=36\pi^2A\); its first-order variation is the missing information.
- Bare exceptional negative Gram data do not provide that variation. Negative scalar curvature permits their harmonic Bochner identities to be paid by derivative energy.
- No same-family construction beating \(4\) was obtained.
- I independently checked root’s new §1: positivity threshold, conformal stationarity, Bach-flat/Kähler/parallel-Ricci exclusions, and coefficient cancellation are consistent. No mathematical correction identified.

No files were edited.

## 407. 2026-09-27T08:20:21.202Z — multiscale_matching_20260927c

Research thread: `01a0e1dd-8121-70a1-9c7c-32f7b0abeb63`.

The holonomy extension is exact: simultaneous parallel limits are possible only for the odd cyclic quotients
\[
\boxed{\frac1n(1,-2),\qquad n\ \text{odd},}
\]
with two specified Spin-c structures. These are actual local exceptions, so the restriction cannot simply be removed.

**Holonomy classification.** Let a finite group \(\Gamma\subset SO(4)\) act freely on \(S^3\), and let a flat Spin-c lift have nonzero invariant vectors in both \(S^+\) and \(S^-\otimes\det S^+\).

Use the standard presentation
\[
\operatorname{Spin}^c(4)
=\{(A,B)\in U(2)\times U(2):\det A=\det B\},
\]
where \(A,B\) act on the two spinor spaces. This presentation and the determinant character are recorded in [Haydys, Example 121(b)](https://haydys.net/misc/IntroGaugeTheory_LectNotes.pdf).

Choose unitary bases putting both invariant vectors first, and write
\(\lambda=\det A=\det B\). Invariance forces
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda^{-1}&0\\0&\lambda^2\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{L1}
\]
Indeed, invariance in \(S^-\otimes\det S^+\) says that \(B\) has eigenvalue \(\lambda^{-1}\); its other eigenvalue must therefore be \(\lambda^2\).

Identify the real Clifford space with
\[
Q(z_1,z_2)=
\begin{pmatrix}z_1&-\overline z_2\\z_2&\overline z_1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
BQA^{-1}=Q(\lambda^{-1}z_1,\lambda^2z_2).
\tag{L2}
\]
The character \(\lambda\) is faithful: if \(\lambda=1\), both matrices in (L1) are identity, hence so is the tangent action. Thus \(\Gamma\) is cyclic, and its tangent action is
\[
(z_1,z_2)\longmapsto
(\lambda^{-1}z_1,\lambda^2z_2).
\]
This action is free on \(S^3\) precisely when its order \(n\) is odd. For even \(n\), the element \(\lambda=-1\) fixes the second coordinate axis. For odd \(n\), neither eigenvalue of a nonidentity element equals one.

Conversely, every odd cyclic action above admits the lift (L1), with invariant vectors
\[
\Phi_0=e_1,\qquad T_0=e_1,
\]
since
\[
S^-\otimes\det S^+:
\quad \lambda B=\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda^3).
\]
For \(n=3\), the latter representation is entirely trivial and its invariant space has complex dimension two. For every other nontrivial odd \(n\), that dimension is one. The positive invariant space has dimension one.

This classification uses orientation-preserving conjugacy. Reversing one complex plane would change the chirality and is not an additional permitted equivalence.

**Characters in ordinary cyclic-quotient notation.** For
\[
\frac1n(1,q),\qquad
(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(\zeta z_1,\zeta^qz_2),
\]
put \(\delta=\zeta^{1+q}\). Its canonical Spin-c lift is
\[
A_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,\delta),
\qquad
B_0=\operatorname{diag}(\zeta,\zeta^q).
\]
Twisting by a character \(\chi\) gives
\[
A=\chi A_0,\qquad
S^-\otimes\det S^+=\chi^3\delta B_0.
\]
A positive invariant forces \(\chi=1\) or \(\chi=\delta^{-1}\). Either choice admits a negative twisted invariant exactly when
\[
\boxed{q+2\equiv0\pmod n
\quad\text{or}\quad
2q+1\equiv0\pmod n.}
\tag{L3}
\]
These are the two coordinate orders of the same oriented quotient type. They force \(n\) odd. The permitted determinant characters are exactly
\[
\boxed{\delta,\quad\delta^{-1}.}
\tag{L4}
\]
For the standard action \(1/n(1,-2)\), this says that the restricted determinant class is \(\pm1\in H^2(S^3/\Gamma;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z/n\).

Therefore the previously proved annular inequality and all its packing consequences extend:

- To every fixed finite family of free quotient groups outside these odd cyclic types.
- Also to these cyclic types when the actual restricted Spin-c structure has a determinant character other than (L4).

No flat determinant assumption is added. On the fixed annulus, its determinant line is torsion and admits a flat connection; the Coulomb argument identifies the limiting flat lift. The previous critical Rellich/Vitali proof then applies unchanged, with (L1)–(L4) replacing the \(SU(2)_-\) representation contradiction.

**The cyclic exceptions survive the actual local weighted equation.** Here is an explicit construction, including the canonical negative-Einstein weight.

For the lift (L1), consider first the flat rescaled metric on a ball and
\[
\Phi_r^{\rm seed}(y)
=a e_1+r c\,\overline z_1e_2.
\tag{L5}
\]
This is equivariant because \(\overline z_1\) transforms by \(\lambda\). With the inherited Clifford matrices,
\[
C_1=I,\qquad C_2=\operatorname{diag}(i,-i),
\]
its physical derivatives for the metric \(r^2g_{\rm eucl}\) are
\[
P_1=ce_2,\qquad P_2=-ice_2,
\]
and \(C_1P_1+C_2P_2=0\). Thus (L5) is exactly Dirac-harmonic. Its physical cubic torsion is exactly
\[
\boxed{t_{\Phi_r^{\rm seed}}=2a^2c\,e_1.}
\tag{L6}
\]
This follows directly from
\[
t=ac(C_1\Phi-iC_2\Phi)=2a^2c\,e_1;
\]
there is no neglected lower-order term.

Choose
\[
a^2=\rho_\beta,\qquad
c^2=\frac{m_\beta}{4a^4}.
\tag{L7}
\]
At the zero endpoint these become
\[
a^2=\frac43,\qquad c=\frac{\sqrt2}{3},
\qquad |t|^2=\frac{128}{81}.
\]

Now take hyperbolic four-space of sectional curvature \(-1/3\), with \(\Gamma\) acting by the above rotations around a fixed point. In rescaled normal coordinates,
\[
h_r=r^{-2}(\exp_p(r\,\cdot))^*g
=g_{\rm eucl}+O(r^2)
\]
in every fixed smooth norm. The radial spin identification is equivariant, and
\[
D_{h_r,A_{\rm flat}}\Phi_r^{\rm seed}=O(r^2).
\]
Use the same Dirichlet right-inverse construction as the existing local-core proof. On the covering ball, its operators commute with the finite group action. Their curved versions remain uniformly bounded by the \(O(r^2)\) Neumann perturbation argument.

Writing the determinant connection as \(A_{\rm flat}+\alpha\), the contraction is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha(\Phi)
&=R_A\!\left(0,\sqrt2\,r^2i\,2\sigma_{h_r}(\Phi)\right),\\
\mathcal T(\Phi)
&=\Phi_r^{\rm seed}
-R_D\!\left(
D_{h_r,A_{\rm flat}}\Phi_r^{\rm seed}
+\frac12c_{h_r}(\alpha(\Phi))\Phi\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
It preserves equivariance and has Lipschitz constant \(O(r^2)\) on a fixed neighborhood. Its smooth fixed point satisfies
\[
\|\Phi_r-\Phi_r^{\rm seed}\|_{C^k}
+\|\alpha_r\|_{C^k}\le C_kr^2.
\]
After returning to physical scale and restricting to the free quotient annulus, this gives the actual equations
\[
D_A\Phi=0,\qquad F_A^+=2i\sigma_g(\Phi),
\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}_g=-g,\quad W_g^\pm=0.
\tag{L8}
\]
The canonical majorant is exactly \(f_0=2\).

The physical estimates on a fixed-ratio annulus are
\[
\begin{gathered}
\rho=\rho_\beta+O(r^2),\qquad
t=2a^2c\,e_1+O(r),\\
\zeta=O(r),\qquad |F_A|=O(1),\qquad
\mathcal A=O(r^2).
\end{gathered}
\tag{L9}
\]
Here \(d=O(r^2)\) follows from the actual Dirac decomposition, and
\(S-2m_\beta=O(r)\), hence \(J=O(r^2)\).

Consequently all three terms in the proposed annular lower bound tend to zero:
\[
r^{-4}\int\mathcal A\longrightarrow0,\qquad
\int|F_A|^2\longrightarrow0,\qquad
r^{-8/3}\int|D_{3A}t|^{4/3}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{L10}
\]
For the last assertion, rescaled \(C^1\) convergence of \(t\) already suffices. The actual prolonged equation gives the stronger physical estimate
\(|D_{3A}t|=O(r)\).

The construction can be performed equivariantly on the entire covering ball and then restricted to punctured quotient annuli with arbitrarily large radius ratio. Thus these exceptions can carry nonzero approximately calibrated physical torsion across long local quotient necks.

This is a sharp exception to the annular obstruction. It does not provide a smooth filling of the quotient singularity, a closed manifold, or the global actual-class and endpoint budgets.

## 409. 2026-09-27T08:27:16.846Z — local_smoothing_euler_20260927c

Research thread: `01a0e1dd-19b8-7312-bd57-3e583e0d63ad`.

Proof closure: I found no analytic blocker in §3. The new Euler-density theorem uses only the stated bounded-Ricci hypothesis, fixed-scale covering charts, and bounded-form defects.

Two statement-level clarifications should be explicit: \(M\) is closed, oriented, smooth, and four-dimensional; \(t\in[0,1/4]\) is a **constant parameter**. The latter matters in the Bianchi calculation.

### Classical hypotheses and local charts

I re-read Cheeger–Tian’s original Theorem 0.8. Its energy hypothesis concerns one ball \(B_r(x)\), with \(r\le1\), and requires compact closures of the smaller balls. It does not import Theorem 0.1’s total-energy or global-collapse assumptions. Closedness supplies the closure condition.

Remark 8.22 explicitly replaces Einsteinness by bounded Ricci and replaces pointwise curvature control by covering \(C^{1,\alpha}/W^{2,q}\) geometry. Remarks 2.7 and 4.8 identify actual local covering spaces and harmonic coordinates. Thus composing an upstairs chart with its projection supplies the local diffeomorphism in (3.3). The controlled metric is the pullback of **original \(g\)**, not merely a comparison metric. [Cheeger–Tian, printed pp.489, 501, 507, 515](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/Courses/MAT683/201001/MAT683S10.pdf).

Rescaling gives \(|\mathrm{Ric}_{r^{-2}g}|\le Kr^2\le K\), and the four-dimensional curvature integral is invariant. The resulting chart radius and regularity constants are uniform after fixing \(K,r\). No scale invariance of \(Z_t\) is needed.

### Independent audit of local coercivity

The precise CT charts allow a direct proof, bypassing any concern about applying a globally stated Cheeger–Naber theorem to an incomplete domain.

Fix \(q>4\), retaining the source’s \(C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,q}\) chart bounds. Suppose the buffered integrals of \(Z_{t_i}\) tend to zero.

1. On a fixed Euclidean subball, extract \(C^{1,\alpha'}\) and weak \(W^{2,q}\) metric convergence. Since
   \[
   |\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i}+g_i|_{g_i}\le K+2,
   \]
   the vanishing \(L^2\) residual also vanishes in every finite \(L^p\), by interpolation.

2. The harmonic-coordinate metric equation passes to the limit and gives \(\mathrm{Ric}_{g_\infty}=-g_\infty\). Interior elliptic regularity makes the limit smooth. Subtracting the metric equations gives strong interior \(W^{2,q}\) convergence, hence strong \(L^2\) Weyl convergence. **No derivative of Ricci is estimated.**

3. Self-duality gives \(\delta_{g_i}\omega_i=-*_{g_i}d\omega_i\). Uniform interior estimates for \(d+\delta\), available from the controlled chart metrics, give an \(H^1\) bound. Rellich yields strong \(L^2\) convergence. The amplitude bound upgrades the quadratic \(\omega_i\)-model to strong \(L^2\) convergence.

4. The limit is self-dual, closed, coclosed, and has squared norm two. With the smooth limit metric, elliptic regularity makes it smooth. Thus the exact system (8.3) follows.

For \(t_\infty=0\), Armstrong’s exclusion is genuinely **local**: his Theorem 3.3.5 and preceding pp.70–72 argument contain no compactness hypothesis. ASD Einstein almost-Kähler geometry must be Kähler; ASD Kähler then has scalar zero, contradicting \(s=-4\). This is not an invocation of the unresolved general Goldberg conjecture. [Armstrong, Theorem 3.3.5](https://johnarmstrongmaths.com/publications/resources/thesis.pdf).

For \(t_\infty>0\), apply Einstein Bianchi only to the smooth limit:
\[
0=\nabla^iW^+_{ijkl}
=-c\,t_\infty\,\omega_{ij}\nabla^i\omega_{kl},
\]
where the harmless nonzero constant depends on tensor/operator conventions. Constant length and coclosedness eliminate the other terms. Nondegeneracy of \(\omega\) forces \(\nabla\omega=0\). Weitzenböck and the model eigenvalue then give
\[
-\frac23\omega=W^+\omega=-\frac{4t_\infty}{3}\omega,
\]
so \(t_\infty=1/2\), impossible.

Consequently the local coercivity constant is uniform over the entire closed interval \([0,1/4]\).

### Buffered polar integration and Liouville transfer

For \(\rho=ar/(8\sqrt Q)\), ellipticity places the closed \(4\rho\)-ball inside the compact Euclidean subball of radius \(ar/2\). Therefore geodesics of length at most \(2\rho\) exist, and minimizing geodesics/polar integration are available despite the chart domain’s incompleteness.

Before the upstairs cut time, Ricci lower comparison gives the radial Jacobian bound \(C_Js^3\). Removing the cut restriction **after** this bound is legitimate by nonnegativity. Local isometries project geodesics to original-\(g\) geodesics, producing precisely (3.5).

The resulting right side is a single measurable function of the downstairs center. It contains no choice of charts. Integrating it over \(G\), enlarging to \(M\), and using the original geodesic flow’s Liouville invariance is valid. No measurable chart selection, sheet bound, covering degree, or injectivity downstairs enters.

The Euler/Fubini/Markov step then gives the required half-volume set exactly as written.

### Bottom line

There is no hidden need for:

- derivatives of Ricci;
- a pointwise full-curvature bound;
- base noncollapse or a volume lower bound;
- a global covering space;
- a complete smoothed comparison metric;
- small energy at every center.

I recommend inserting the direct chart-compactness paragraph above, or a shortened version, to make this central theorem independently checkable without relying solely on the inherited buffered-localization assertion. The proof itself closes under the stated hypotheses. No files changed.

## 410. 2026-09-27T08:41:07.167Z — local_smoothing_euler_20260927c

Research thread: `01a0e1dd-19b8-7312-bd57-3e583e0d63ad`.

Confirmed: the Euler premise is automatic on the classical general-type surgery family, and the raw-form theorem admits the proposed topology-ratio replacement.

### Noether verification and automatic bounds

[Liedtke, Theorem 2.1, printed p.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702548), states
\[
K_X^2\ge2p_g(X)-4
\]
for every minimal surface of general type. The main inequality requires neither \(q=0\), an ample canonical bundle, nor a particular canonical map.

The formulas \(A=K_X^2\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \(\chi_h=1-q+p_g\), and \(\chi(X)=12\chi_h-A\) are also recorded together in [Bauer–Catanese–Pignatelli, printed p.5](https://www.mathe8.uni-bayreuth.de/de/team/prof-fabrizio-catanese-old/pdf/101.pdf). Consequently,
\[
\chi(X)\le5A+36,\qquad \frac{\chi(X)}A\le41.
\]

For
\[
M=X\#k\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}\#\ell(S^1\times S^3),
\qquad h=\frac{k+4\ell}{A}\le\frac13,
\]
the exact surgery identities give
\[
\chi(M)=\chi(X)+k-2\ell,\qquad T_+(M)=A(1-h).
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{\chi(M)}A\le41+h<42,\qquad
       \frac{\chi(M)}{T_+(M)}
       \le\frac{41+h}{1-h}\le62.}
\]

The inherited polarized construction supplies \(p\ge A\), including its specified \(b_+=1\) chamber and handle insertions. Moreover,
\[
a_H^2=A-k\ge \frac23A>0,
\]
so \(b_a=0\) automatically in this range.

Thus the bounded-Ricci full-pencil estimate has constant \(c(K)\), without a separate Euler premise or square-cost factor. Its pointwise version has a universal constant:
\[
\boxed{\delta_-^2+D_\beta/V
 \ge c\,\frac{(\beta-2)^2}{\beta^2},
 \qquad 2\le\beta<\infty.}
\]
For \(\delta_-\le1/4\), use \(K\le5/2\); for larger \(\delta_-\), decrease \(c\) and use \(D_\beta\ge0\). Hence this statement covers all smooth metrics on these manifolds. The uniform endpoint gap and upper-wall margin follow.

If “entire surgery family” includes \(h\ge1/3\), the already established polarized obstruction gives \(\mathcal E\ge\varepsilon\) there, hence \(r_{\rm Ric}\ge\varepsilon\) and \(\delta_-^2\ge\varepsilon/4\). That handles the remaining surgeries without new geometry.

### Raw-form topology replacement

Put \(z=\fint Z_t\) and \(m=|\omega|^2\). Directly from the defects,
\[
\|m-2\|_{2,\mathrm{avg}}\le\sqrt z,\quad
\|s+4\|_{2,\mathrm{avg}}\le2\sqrt z,\quad P/V\le z.
\]
Since \(|A_{\omega,t}|^2=(2/3)t^2m^2\), Cauchy–Schwarz and chiral Chern–Weil give the explicit bound
\[
\boxed{\left|
\frac{4\pi^2T_+}{V}
-\left(\frac23+\frac{16t^2}{3}\right)
\right|\le3\sqrt z+4z.}
\]
This numerical estimate does not itself need the amplitude bound; that bound remains necessary in the geometric coercivity theorem.

Thus, for sufficiently small \(z\),
\[
T_+>0,\qquad \frac13\le\frac{4\pi^2T_+}{V}\le\frac43.
\]
If \(\chi/T_+\le B\), then
\[
\frac{8\pi^2\chi}{V}\le\frac83\max\{B,0\},
\]
so the Euler theorem applies. This proves
\[
\fint Z_t\ge c(K,L,B)>0
\]
without an actual projection or volume premise.

For \(T_+\le0\), there is the stronger elementary estimate
\[
P\ge S_2/12,\qquad
r_{\rm Ric}
=\fint\left(|\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2+\frac{(s+4)^2}{4}\right)
\ge1+\frac13\fint(s+3)^2\ge1.
\]

Hence every fixed oriented topology has a bounded-Ricci/bounded-amplitude zero-end gap. Across varying topologies, a zero-end sequence must eventually have \(T_+>0\) and \(\chi/T_+\to+\infty\).

Finite-cover degrees introduce no new ratio loss: both \(\chi\) and \(T_+\) multiply by the degree. This observation does not supply any additional twisted gauge-solvability input.

The unrestricted integral-Ricci endpoint remains open. No files changed.

## 412. 2026-09-27T08:57:53.419Z — resonant_filling_20260927d

Research thread: `01a0e20f-eda0-7d01-8f36-edbf2fe173be`.

A rigorous obstruction is available without classifying Ricci-flat ALE spaces.

**Proposition — faithful flat line obstruction.** Let \(X^m\), \(m\ge3\), be smooth, connected, complete, with \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge0\), and ALE with nontrivial group \(\Gamma\) at infinity. No flat unitary line bundle on \(X\) restricts to a faithful holonomy character of \(\Gamma\).

Here is a self-contained proof. Write \(N=|\Gamma|\); the asymptotic volume ratio of \(X\) is \(1/N\). Let \(\widetilde X\) be its universal cover and \(D\) a Dirichlet domain centered at \(\tilde p\). For any finite set \(S\) of deck transformations, with maximum displacement \(a\),

\[
|S|\operatorname{Vol}B_X(p,R)
\le \operatorname{Vol}B_{\widetilde X}(\tilde p,R+a)
\le \omega_m(R+a)^m .
\]

The first inequality uses the disjoint translates of \(D\cap B(\tilde p,R)\). Dividing by \(\omega_mR^m\) and taking \(R\to\infty\) gives \(|S|\le N\). Thus \(\pi_1(X)\) is finite, of order \(d\le N\).

If a global flat character \(\rho:\pi_1(X)\to U(1)\) restricts faithfully to \(\Gamma=\pi_1(X\setminus K)\), then the inclusion \(\Gamma\to\pi_1(X)\) is injective. Hence \(d\ge N\), so \(d=N\). Finite coverings multiply asymptotic volume ratios, giving

\[
\operatorname{AVR}(\widetilde X)=d/N=1.
\]

Bishop–Gromov rigidity makes \(\widetilde X\) Euclidean. A nontrivial finite group of Euclidean isometries cannot act freely: averaging an orbit produces a fixed point. Contradiction.

This argument needs neither spinors nor Kähler geometry. For the Ricci-flat ALE covering facts, [Șuvaina, Lemmas 4.1–4.2 and Remark 4.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.2672) supplies an independent primary-source route.

**Corollary — the resonant oriented cones have no positive-parallel-spinor filling.** For odd \(n>1\), there is no smooth complete Ricci-flat ALE four-manifold with physically oriented infinity

\[
\Gamma_n=\frac1n(1,-2)
\]

and a nonzero global parallel positive Spin-c spinor.

Flatness of the determinant connection is automatic. If \(F_A=i\Omega\), the parallel-spinor curvature identity is

\[
\operatorname{Ric}(v)\cdot\Phi
=i(v\mathbin{\lrcorner}\Omega)\cdot\Phi .
\]

Since \(\operatorname{Ric}=0\) and Clifford multiplication by a nonzero real covector is invertible, \(\Omega=0\). This is [Moroianu, Lemma 3.1, PDF p. 4](https://moroianu.perso.math.cnrs.fr/tex/1997cmp.pdf); only its local identity is needed.

At infinity, the parallel spinor limits to a nonzero invariant positive spinor. In the marking used by current §4.1, write \(\delta=\zeta^{-1}\). Every lift has

\[
S^+=\chi\,\operatorname{diag}(1,\delta).
\]

An invariant vector forces \(\chi=1\) or \(\delta^{-1}\), so its determinant character is \(\delta\) or \(\delta^{-1}\). Both are faithful. The proposition excludes either case. Thus the negative twisted spinor need not extend through the core.

Consequently, **no Ricci-flat Kähler ALE filling exists in the specified orientation for \(n>1\)**: its canonical Spin-c structure has a parallel positive spinor. When \(n=1\), Bishop–Gromov gives only flat \(\mathbb R^4\).

Șuvaina’s classification corroborates this. The nontrivial cyclic Kähler possibilities have

\[
N=dk^2,\qquad q=dkm-1,\qquad (k,m)=1,
\]

whose determinant character has order \(k\), whereas \(q=-2\) has determinant order \(N\). Equality would force \(dk=1\), hence \(N=1\). See [Șuvaina, Theorem B and Theorem 2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.2672).

The orientation qualification is essential. Reversing the \(n=3\) cone produces the \(A_2\) cone \(1/3(1,-1)\); reversing \(n=9\) produces the type-T cone \(1/9(1,2)\). These admit Ricci-flat Kähler fillings with the opposite orientation.

Your APS calculation also checks out. With outward-boundary convention

\[
\tau=\frac1{12\pi^2}\int(|W^+|^2-|W^-|^2)-\eta,
\]

one has

\[
\eta(L(n,-2))=\frac{(n-1)(n-5)}{6n},\qquad
B_n=\frac2n-3\eta=3-\frac n2-\frac1{2n}.
\]

These signs agree with [Wright, Proposition 6.2 and the cotangent formula, PDF pp. 44 and 49](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/alumni/2013-Evan-Wright.pdf). Therefore

\[
2\chi+3\tau-B_n
=\frac1{4\pi^2}\int
\left(2|W^+|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}|^2}{2}\right),
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{dist}(B_n,\mathbb Z)
=\frac{n-1}{2n}\ge\frac13.
\]

Thus Ricci-flat ASD fillings are excluded even without Spin-c data; your proposed signed-integral and absolute-cost consequences follow with the stated constants.

The legitimate degeneration consequence is precise: once the **same actual limit** is smooth, complete, Ricci-flat ALE, has resonant oriented infinity, and carries a nonzero global parallel positive Spin-c limit, it is impossible. This removes the first-order expansion, finite first-order curvature energy, bounded first-order derivative, and global parallel-frame assumptions from that filling exclusion. It does not supply ALE compactness or identify an escaping annulus with that same limit.

A smaller correction to the earlier §7 is also justified: on its already globally hyperkähler background, the global-frame hypothesis follows from its nonzero parallel positive spinor. The adjoint holonomy on \(\Lambda^+\) is trivial, so positive-spinor holonomy is scalar; fixing the spinor forces that scalar to be \(1\). Likewise \(H^1(X;\mathbb R)=0\) follows from finite \(\pi_1(X)\).

No files were edited.

A genuine conditional bridge is available. It replaces pointwise Ricci control by a small, scale-normalized integral lower-Ricci condition **within an explicitly elliptic class**. It does not cover arbitrary Yamabe metrics or the unrestricted integral endpoint.

Everything below is read-only; no files were changed.

**Proposed theorem.** Fix \(p>2\), \(r_0\in(0,1]\), \(A,L<\infty\), and \(\Lambda_0\). Define
\[
 \rho_-(x)=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\operatorname{Ric}^{\sharp}(x))\},\qquad
 k_p(r)=r^2\sup_x\left(\fint_{B_r(x)}\rho_-^p\right)^{1/p}.
\]
There is \(\delta_p>0\) such that the following hypotheses on a closed oriented four-manifold imply
\[
 \fint_M Z_t\ge c(p,r_0,A,L,\Lambda_0)>0:
\]
\[
 |\nabla^*\nabla\operatorname{Ric}|
       \le A|\operatorname{Rm}|\,|\operatorname{Ric}|,\qquad
 k_p(r_0)\le\delta_p,\qquad
 |\omega|\le L,\qquad
 \frac{8\pi^2\chi(M)}{V}\le\Lambda_0.
\]
Here \(\omega\) is smooth and self-dual, \(0\le t\le1/4\), and \(Z_t\) is exactly I45 (3.1). There is no diameter or noncollapse assumption. \(\operatorname{Rm}\) below uses the full four-index norm.

The elliptic inequality is a genuine additional input. It holds for constant-scalar-curvature critical points of \(Q_\tau=R+\tau S_2\), uniformly when \(|\tau|\) is bounded.

The proof can be made explicit as follows.

1. **Comparison and normalized Sobolev input.**

   Choose \(\delta_p\) sufficiently small that [Dai–Wei–Zhang, Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.5, equations (2.5)–(2.6)](https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~wei/paper/Dai-Wei-Zhang.pdf) apply at every scale at most \(r_0\). Their statements are expressly valid in the collapsed setting. They give
   \[
   \frac{\operatorname{Vol}B_a(x)}{\operatorname{Vol}B_b(x)}
      \ge\frac12(a/b)^4,\qquad 0<a\le b\le r_0.
   \tag{A}
   \]
   Consequently,
   \[
   \operatorname{Vol}B_r(x)\le2\omega_4r^4,\qquad
   \operatorname{Vol}B_{2r}(x)\le32\operatorname{Vol}B_r(x).
   \tag{B}
   \]
   The first follows by letting \(a\downarrow0\) in (A).

   Whenever \(B_{2r}(x)\) is proper, their Sobolev inequality, applied to \(|f|^3\), gives
   \[
   \left(\fint_{B_r}|f|^4\right)^{1/2}
       \le S(p)r^2\fint_{B_r}|\nabla f|^2,
       \qquad f\in C_c^\infty(B_r).
   \tag{C}
   \]
   No unnormalized Sobolev constant is claimed to remain bounded.

2. **The precise normalized elliptic lemma.**

   Under (C) and the elliptic Ricci inequality, there are \(e_0,C_R>0\), depending only on \(p,A\), such that
   \[
   r^4\fint_{B_r}|\operatorname{Rm}|^2\le e_0
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
   \sup_{B_{r/8}}|\operatorname{Ric}|
       \le C_R\left(\fint_{B_r}|\operatorname{Ric}|^2\right)^{1/2}.
   \tag{D}
   \]
   This is the normalized version of only the early estimates in [Tian–Viaclovsky, Section 3, Lemmas 3.2–3.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0310302), preceding their volume-comparison step. It does not invoke a collapsed harmonic-radius theorem.

   Here is the normalization check and analytic derivation. Set
   \[
   h=r^{-2}g,\qquad d\nu=\frac{dV_g}{\operatorname{Vol}_g B_r}.
   \]
   Thus \(\nu(B_1^h)=1\), and (C) becomes
   \[
   \|f\|_{4,\nu}^2\le S\|\nabla_h f\|_{2,\nu}^2.
   \]
   Multiplying Riemannian measure by a constant preserves integration by parts.

   Write \(U=\operatorname{Ric}_h\), \(B=\operatorname{Rm}_h\). Kato’s inequality, a cutoff, and Hölder give
   \[
   \|\phi U\|_{4,\nu}^2
     \le C(A)S\|B\|_{2,\nu}\|\phi U\|_{4,\nu}^2
          +C(A,S)\|U\|_{2,\nu}^2.
   \]
   Absorption and the tensor energy identity yield, on a smaller ball,
   \[
   \|U\|_{4,\nu}^2+\|\nabla U\|_{2,\nu}^2
      \le C\|U\|_{2,\nu}^2.
   \tag{E}
   \]
   The universal curvature identity
   \[
   \Delta B=\mathcal L(\nabla^2U)+B*B
   \]
   gives, after one integration by parts,
   \[
   \int\psi^2|\nabla B|^2\,d\nu
      \le C\!\int(|\nabla\psi|^2|B|^2+\psi^2|\nabla U|^2)\,d\nu
        +C\!\int\psi^2|B|^3\,d\nu.
   \]
   Applying (C), (E), and absorption again gives
   \[
       \|B\|_{4,\nu;B_{1/2}}^2
                 \le C\|B\|_{2,\nu;B_1}^2.
   \tag{F}
   \]
   Finally \(u=|U|\) satisfies \(\Delta u\ge-A|B|u\). For \(v=\psi u^{m/2}\), the potential term is estimated by
   \[
   \int |B|v^2\,d\nu
       \le\|B\|_{4,\nu}\|v\|_{8/3,\nu}^2
       \le\|B\|_{4,\nu}\|v\|_{2,\nu}\|v\|_{4,\nu}.
   \]
   Young’s inequality and (C) produce
   \[
   \|u\|_{2m,B_a}
      \le\big[C\{m^4+m^2(b-a)^{-2}\}\big]^{1/m}
             \|u\|_{m,B_b}.
   \]
   Iteration proves \(\sup_{B_{1/8}}|U|\le C_R\|U\|_{2,\nu}\). Rescaling gives (D). All integrals here use the same \(\nu\); no missing volume factor appears.

3. **Selecting regular centers using Euler density.**

   Put \(z=\fint Z_t\). We may assume \(z\le1\). Then
   \[
   \fint|\operatorname{Ric}|^2\le10,\qquad
   \fint|\operatorname{Rm}|^2
       =\frac{32\pi^2\chi}{V}+4\fint|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}|^2
       \le H:=4(1+\max\{\Lambda_0,0\}).
   \tag{G}
   \]

   For any nonnegative \(F\), doubling in (B) gives the exact averaging estimate
   \[
   \fint_M\fint_{B_r(x)}F(y)\,d\mu(y)d\mu(x)
        \le32\fint_M F.
   \tag{H}
   \]
   Indeed, for \(x\in B_r(y)\),
   \[
   \operatorname{Vol}B_r(y)
       \le\operatorname{Vol}B_{2r}(x)
       \le32\operatorname{Vol}B_r(x).
   \]

   Decrease \(e_0\) so that \(e_0\le1\) and
   \[
      2\omega_4 e_0
             <\epsilon_{\rm CT}(C_R+1)
   \tag{I}
   \]
   in the full-tensor convention. Choose
   \[
   R=\min\left\{\frac{r_0}{64},\,1,\,
                    \left(\frac{e_0}{2^{20}H}\right)^{1/4}\right\}.
   \tag{J}
   \]

   First suppose \(D=\operatorname{diam}M\ge8R\). All \(B_{2R}(x)\) are proper. By (G)–(H), at least half the centers satisfy
   \[
       R^4\fint_{B_R(x)}|\operatorname{Rm}|^2\le e_0.
   \]
   At such a center (D) gives
   \[
       |\operatorname{Ric}|
            \le C_R\sqrt{e_0}\,R^{-2}
                  \quad\hbox{on }B_{R/8}(x).
   \tag{K}
   \]
   Meanwhile (B) gives
   \[
       \int_{B_R(x)}|\operatorname{Rm}|^2
                  \le2\omega_4 e_0.
   \tag{L}
   \]
   Apply the original bounded-Ricci Cheeger–Tian input on \(B_{R/16}(x)\). After scaling that ball to unit size, the Ricci bound in (K) is at most \(C_R/256\), and (I)–(L) supply its unnormalized small-energy premise.

   Thus a positive volume fraction has the same buffered covering charts used by I45. The local coercivity and Liouville-measure averaging argument of I45 then gives \(z\ge c>0\).

   Only the Ricci bounds inside these good neighborhoods enter radial Jacobian comparison. Extending a nonnegative angular integral from good centers to all centers does not require a global Ricci bound.

4. **The small-diameter case does not introduce a hidden diameter premise.**

   Suppose \(D<8R\), and put \(u=D/16\). Every \(B_{2u}(x)\) is proper. Since \(B_{2D}(x)=M\), (A) gives
   \[
      \operatorname{Vol}B_u(x)\ge\frac{V}{2\cdot32^4}.
   \tag{M}
   \]
   Thus every center satisfies
   \[
   u^4\fint_{B_u(x)}|\operatorname{Rm}|^2
       \le32D^4H
       \le2^{17}R^4H
       \le e_0/8.
   \]
   Applying (D) at every center and using (G), (M),
   \[
   |\operatorname{Ric}|(x)
       \le C_R\sqrt{20\cdot32^4},
   \]
   a global bound independent of \(D\). The already established I45 theorem now applies directly. This completes the bridge.

For actual gauge supply, the same \(z\le C(r_{\rm Ric}+D_\beta/V)+o(1)\) gives
\[
 r_{\rm Ric}+D_\beta/V\ge c,\qquad \beta\ge4,
\]
under the new elliptic and integral-local hypotheses. The topological replacement of Euler density in I45 §3.6 still works: its Chern–Weil calculation uses bounded amplitude and small \(z\), not Ricci \(L^\infty\).

**The stationary class is verified, but Yamabe replacement alone is insufficient.** At constant scalar curvature, [Catino, Section 2, equation (2.1)](https://www.mate.polimi.it/wp-content/themes/mymate/send_new.php?file=qdd205&tipo=1) gives
\[
 \Delta\operatorname{Ric}
   =-2\operatorname{Rm}(\operatorname{Ric})
     -2\tau s\,\operatorname{Ric}
     +\tfrac12(|\operatorname{Ric}|^2+\tau s^2)g.
\]
Hence the elliptic inequality holds with \(A\le C(1+|\tau|)\). For the I45 stationary connection, \(\tau=-1/(4-\mathcal E)\in(-1/3,-1/4]\) when \(0\le\mathcal E<1\), so \(A\) is uniform. A negative Yamabe representative only supplies constant scalar curvature; it need not satisfy this tensor equation. An arbitrary minimizing sequence is not a sequence of critical points.

Also, small \(k_p(r_0)\) is **not derived from the actual endpoint budgets**. Global normalized \(L^2\) convergence cannot control the local \(L^p\) averages divided by potentially tiny ball volumes.

A useful necessary escape statement follows: for an elliptic actual endpoint sequence with bounded Euler density and amplitude, for each fixed \(p>2\) and \(r>0\),
\[
 \liminf_j k_p^{g_j}(r)\ge\delta_p.
\]
A diagonal choice gives radii \(r_j\downarrow0\) and centers \(x_j\) with
\[
 r_j^{2p}\fint_{B_{r_j}(x_j)}\rho_{-,j}^p
                       \ge(\delta_p/2)^p.
\]
This is a local normalized Ricci concentration requirement, not an unnormalized bubble-energy bound.

**Concrete obstruction to simply replacing CT’s pointwise bound by a bounded \(L^p\) budget.** The warped-neck construction discussed in [Dai–Wei–Zhang, Section 6](https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~wei/paper/Dai-Wei-Zhang.pdf) admits the following closed version.

On \(T^4=S^1\times T^3\), take
\[
 g_\varepsilon=dr^2+f_\varepsilon(r)^2g_{T^3},\qquad
 f_\varepsilon(r)=(\varepsilon^2+r^2)^{a/2}
\]
near \(r=0\), patched smoothly to a fixed positive function away from zero. Choose
\[
 a>1,\qquad 3a+1>2p.
\]
Near the neck,
\[
 \frac{f'}f=\frac{ar}{\varepsilon^2+r^2},\qquad
 \frac{f''}f
     =\frac{a[\varepsilon^2+(a-1)r^2]}
                 {(\varepsilon^2+r^2)^2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 |\operatorname{Ric}|+|\operatorname{Rm}|
       \asymp_a(\varepsilon^2+r^2)^{-1},\qquad
 dV=(\varepsilon^2+r^2)^{3a/2}\,dr\,dV_{T^3}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \sup_\varepsilon\int_M|\operatorname{Ric}|^p<\infty,
 \qquad
 \int_{|r|<u}|\operatorname{Rm}|^2
                   \le C_a u^{3a-3}\quad(\varepsilon\le u).
\]
Volume is bounded above and below, and \(\chi(T^4)=0\). At every fixed radius, ball volumes have a uniform positive lower bound depending on that radius, so the fixed-scale normalized local \(L^p\) Ricci budget is also uniformly bounded.

Nevertheless no uniformly elliptic, uniformly \(W^{2,q}\) covering charts of fixed radius can exist at the neck for any \(q>2\). Such a chart contains a coordinate neighborhood of radius comparable to \(\varepsilon\), with volume comparable to \(\varepsilon^4\). Its image has \(|r|\lesssim\varepsilon\), hence \(|\operatorname{Ric}|\gtrsim\varepsilon^{-2}\). Consequently
\[
 \int_{\rm chart}|\operatorname{Ric}|^q
                     \gtrsim\varepsilon^{4-2q}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
contradicting the Ricci \(L^q\) bound supplied by uniform ellipticity and a \(W^{2,q}\) metric bound.

Thus even a bounded supercritical Ricci budget, bounded Euler density, and small unnormalized local curvature energy do not justify CT covering regularity after dropping pointwise Ricci control. This example is a regularity obstruction, not an actual-field endpoint counterexample.

## 414. 2026-09-27T09:09:03.126Z — resonant_filling_20260927d

Research thread: `01a0e20f-eda0-7d01-8f36-edbf2fe173be`.

Reviewed §§1–2. The constants, incoming-boundary signs, binary branching bound, and \(C\delta^2/n\) flattening estimate are correct. The Weyl norm clarification has now been incorporated: these are Hilbert–Schmidt norms.

The flattening proof genuinely gives an additive error independent of \(n\): the modified lifted annulus has curvature \(O(\delta)\), bounded lifted volume, and quotient volume smaller by \(n\). Its unchanged interior requires no comparison of different curvature norms. The small-volume absorption in (1.10)–(1.11) is also valid.

The signed formula gives substantially stronger actual consequences. Write

\[
e=\int_\Omega Z_t,\quad v=\operatorname{Vol}(\Omega),\quad
f=\frac{n-1}{2n},\quad
j=2\chi+3\tau-\lfloor B_n\rfloor,\quad
b_L=\frac23+\frac{L^4}{12}.
\]

For an approximately conical collar, put \(\epsilon=C\delta^2/n\), so

\[
\left|\int_\Omega
\left(2|W^+|^2+\frac{s^2}{24}-\frac{|\mathrm{Ric}^\circ|^2}{2}\right)
-4\pi^2(j-f)\right|\le\epsilon .
\]

Then:

- If \(j\le0\),
  \[
  \int_\Omega|\mathrm{Ric}+g|^2
  \ge8\pi^2(f-j)-2\epsilon.
  \]
  No volume, form-amplitude, gauge, or \(W^+\) assumption is needed. Minimal-resolution cores have \(j=0\), giving a concrete pure-Ricci application.
- If \(j\ge1\),
  \[
  e\ge\frac12
  \left[
  \sqrt{\bigl(4\pi^2(j-f)-\epsilon\bigr)_+}
  -\sqrt{b_Lv}
  \right]_+^2.
  \]
  This follows from \(L^2\) Minkowski applied to
  \((\sqrt2W^+,s/\sqrt{24})\), separating its bounded model from its defect.

Thus \(v\to0,\delta\to0\) forces a defect contribution at least \(\pi^2\), uniformly over varying odd \(n\). Fixed \(n\) gives at least \(\pi^2(1+1/n)\), or \(4\pi^2(1-1/n)\) on the \(j\le0\) branch. These are local exclusions and concentration bounds requiring no decomposition theorem. Vanishing *normalized* defect still permits finitely many cores when total volume diverges.

Your Calderbank–Singer sharpness argument is valid. [Theorem A and §4.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0206229) provide smooth scalar-flat Kähler ALE metrics on the minimal resolution. Positive ALE decay suffices: flatten on \([R,2R]\), pay \(o(1)\), and retain the interior energy tending to \(8\pi^2f\). No specific numerical decay order or uniform truncation radius across \(n\) is required. An additional homothety makes volume vanish and also gives
\(\int|\mathrm{Ric}+g|^2\to8\pi^2f\). This establishes metric-cap sharpness, without claiming actual weighted-SW realization or attainment.

Orbifold qualification remains essential: the flat quotient ball with its singular apex has zero curvature cost. Its missing inner boundary contribution cancels the outer term. Smooth original cores still pay the full cost before any singular limit; remaining orbifold points cannot be silently treated as filled.

The Cotton calculation also checks. Use explicitly
\(\Delta=\operatorname{tr}\nabla^2\), unlike the positive Laplacian in the preceding continuation. [Catino, Propositions 2.1 and 4.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1404.0569) give

\[
\Delta Z=-2\mathrm{Rm}(Z)-2bZ+\frac{|Z|^2}{2}g,
\qquad
\frac12\int|C|^2
=\int\sum_{i<j}(\lambda_i+\lambda_j)^2\sec_{ij}+2bP.
\]

Complementary-plane pairing yields exactly

\[
\int(K^\perp_{\max}+\kappa)_+|Z|^2
\ge(\kappa-b)P+\frac14\int|C|^2.
\]

Define \(K^\perp\) as the half-sum of complementary sectional curvatures. At \(\kappa=b\), strict positivity requires further information: the identity alone permits Cotton-flat equality. Choosing \(\kappa>b\), particularly \(1/3\), avoids that issue.

No files were edited.

## 415. 2026-09-27T09:11:44.164Z — sharp_coefficient_20260927d

Research thread: `01a0e210-271d-7983-ae8e-336d0a3a379e`.

The strongest new conclusion is an explicit restriction on smooth extremizers: on the balanced small-\(h\) family, any sequence of smooth attained minima, normalized by \(s=-4\), satisfies
\[
\liminf\|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}\|_{\infty,\mathrm{HS}}^2\ge\frac18,
\qquad
\liminf\frac{\int|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}|^4}
                   {\int|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}|^2}\ge\frac18.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\liminf\|\operatorname{Ric}^{\sharp}+I\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}
\ge\frac1{4\sqrt2}.
\]
This excludes uniformly pointwise near-Einstein sequences of smooth extremizers. It does not determine the infimum coefficient or exclude concentration and nonattainment.

Here is the complete writeup.

1. Exact decomposition from one ordinary SW solution

Let \(g\) be a closed oriented four-metric with \(s=-4\), and let
\[
D_{\mathcal A}\Phi=0,\qquad -iF_{\mathcal A}^+=\sigma(\Phi)
\]
be one actual ordinary solution. Set
\[
\rho=|\Phi|^2,\quad x=\rho/4,\quad
\omega=\sigma(\Phi),\quad
j=\operatorname{Im}\langle\Phi,\nabla_{\mathcal A}\Phi\rangle.
\]
The normalization is \(|\sigma(\Phi)|^2=\rho^2/8\). The maximum principle gives \(0\le x\le1\). These conventions and the spinor and self-dual-form Weitzenböck identities agree with [LeBrun, equations (5)–(7) and Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0003068).

Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
K&=\int|\nabla_{\mathcal A}\Phi|^2,&
Q&=\int(4-\rho)^2,\\
\Gamma&=\int\left(\frac14|d\rho|^2+|j|^2\right),&
J&=\|F_{\mathcal A}^+-(F_{\mathcal A}^+)_H\|_2^2,\\
W_0&=\frac12\left(\frac{|\omega|^2}{3}I-\omega\otimes\omega\right),&
F&=\int|W^+-W_0|^2,\\
H&=\frac23\int(1-x)^2(2+4x-x^2).
\end{aligned}
\]
All Weyl norms are Hilbert–Schmidt norms of the endomorphisms of \(\Lambda^\pm\). Write
\[
D=D_2=24V+18\int|W^+|^2-72\pi^2p.
\]

Then the following is exact:
\[
\boxed{\frac D{18}=F+\frac{\Gamma}{2}+J+H.} \tag{A}
\]

In particular,
\[
F,J\le D/18,\qquad \Gamma\le D/9,\qquad Q\le2D/3. \tag{B}
\]

Proof. The Hopf-map differential and Dirac equation give
\[
|\nabla\omega|^2
=\frac{\rho}{2}|\nabla_{\mathcal A}\Phi|^2-\frac12|j|^2,
\qquad
|d\omega|^2=\frac14|j|^2. \tag{C}
\]
For an explicit normalization check, use
\[
C_1=I,\quad C_2=\operatorname{diag}(i,-i),\quad
C_3=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C_4=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\-i&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
At \(\Phi=\sqrt\rho\,e_1\), write \(\nabla_i\Phi=(a_i,b_i)\). The Dirac equations are
\[
a_1+ia_2+b_3-ib_4=0,\qquad
b_1-ib_2-a_3-ia_4=0.
\]
Differentiating the quadratic map in the self-dual basis
\[
e^{12}+e^{34},\quad e^{13}-e^{24},\quad e^{14}+e^{23}
\]
gives \((d^*\omega)_i=-\sqrt\rho\,\operatorname{Im}(a_i)/2=-j_i/2\), establishing the second identity in (C). Both identities extend through zeros because the quantities are smooth polynomial expressions.

Pairing the ordinary spinor Weitzenböck equation with \(\rho\Phi\) gives
\[
2\int|d\rho|^2+4\int\rho|\nabla_{\mathcal A}\Phi|^2
=\int(4-\rho)\rho^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
T_\omega:=\int(|\nabla\omega|^2-2|d\omega|^2)
=\frac18\int(4-\rho)\rho^2-\Gamma
=8\int x^2(1-x)-\Gamma. \tag{D}
\]

Put \(a=\int x^2\), \(b=\int x^4\). The self-dual Weitzenböck identity gives
\[
\int\langle W^+\omega,\omega\rangle=T_\omega/2-4a/3.
\]
Since \(|W_0|^2=2x^4/3\), expansion yields
\[
F=\int|W^+|^2+\frac23b+\frac12T_\omega-\frac43a. \tag{E}
\]
Harmonic projection gives \(J=2a-4\pi^2p\). Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
D/18-F
&=J+\frac23(2V-a-b)-T_\omega/2\\
&=J+\Gamma/2
+\int\left(\frac43-\frac{14}{3}x^2+4x^3-\frac23x^4\right)\\
&=J+\Gamma/2+H,
\end{aligned}
\]
proving (A). Finally \(2\le2+4x-x^2\le5\), so
\[
Q/12\le H\le5Q/24,
\]
which proves (B). No normalized form or division by \(\rho\) has been used.

2. Critical equation and its biorthogonal-curvature consequence

Suppose \(g\) smoothly attains \(0<\alpha<1\). The established variational reduction gives \(s=-4\) after scaling and stationarity of
\[
\mathcal Q_t=\int|\operatorname{Ric}|^2+t\int s^2,
\qquad t=-1/(4-\alpha).
\]
Set
\[
Z=\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ},\qquad
P=\int|Z|^2,\qquad
\beta=\frac{\alpha}{4-\alpha}=\frac P{4V}.
\]

Use the curvature convention
\[
R_{ikjl}g^{kl}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij},\qquad
\sec(e_i,e_j)=R_{ijij},
\]
and the rough Laplacian \(\Delta=\nabla^k\nabla_k\), which is nonpositive after integration.

The classical first-variation equation specializes to
\[
\boxed{\Delta Z_{ij}
=-2R_{ikjl}Z_{kl}-2\beta Z_{ij}
+\frac12|Z|^2g_{ij}.} \tag{F}
\]
The input formulas are [Catino, Proposition 2.1 and Proposition 4.1](https://www.mate.polimi.it/wp-content/themes/mymate/send_new.php?file=qdd205&tipo=1), printed pages 5 and 9–10. His theorem requiring \(t\ge-1/4\) is not being applied.

Define Cotton by
\[
C_{ijk}=\nabla_kZ_{ij}-\nabla_jZ_{ik},
\qquad |C|^2=\sum_{i,j,k}C_{ijk}^2.
\]
Pairing (F) with \(Z\) gives
\[
\int|\nabla Z|^2
=2\int R_{ikjl}Z_{ij}Z_{kl}+2\beta P. \tag{G}
\]
Using \(\operatorname{div}Z=0\), integration by parts gives
\[
\int|\nabla Z|^2-\frac12\int|C|^2
=\int\left(R_{ikjl}Z_{ij}Z_{kl}
-\operatorname{tr}Z^3-\frac s4|Z|^2\right).
\]
Thus, in a Ricci eigenframe with eigenvalues \(\lambda_i\) of \(Z\),
\[
\boxed{
\frac12\int|C|^2
=\int\sum_{i<j}(\lambda_i+\lambda_j)^2\sec_{ij}
+2\beta P.} \tag{H}
\]
Indeed,
\[
R_{ikjl}Z_{ij}Z_{kl}+\operatorname{tr}Z^3+\frac s4|Z|^2
=\sum_{i<j}(\lambda_i+\lambda_j)^2\sec_{ij},
\]
because \(\operatorname{Ric}_{ii}=\sum_{j\ne i}\sec_{ij}\).

For a plane \(\Pi\), set
\[
K^\perp(\Pi)=\frac{\sec(\Pi)+\sec(\Pi^\perp)}2,
\qquad k_\perp=\max_\Pi K^\perp(\Pi).
\]
Complementary pairs have equal weights, since \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\). Also
\[
\sum_{i<j}(\lambda_i+\lambda_j)^2=2|Z|^2.
\]
Therefore (H) implies, for every \(\kappa>\beta\),
\[
\boxed{
\int(k_\perp+\kappa)_+|Z|^2
\ge(\kappa-\beta)P+\frac14\int|C|^2.} \tag{I}
\]
In particular, no positive smooth extremizer can satisfy \(k_\perp<-\beta\) everywhere.

3. Combining the actual ordinary solution with stationarity

Let \(w_3^\pm\) denote the maximum eigenvalues of \(W^\pm\). The curvature-operator decomposition gives
\[
k_\perp=-\frac13+\frac12(w_3^++w_3^-).
\]
To verify this, write a unit decomposable form as \((u+v)/\sqrt2\), where \(u\in\Lambda^+\), \(v\in\Lambda^-\) are unit forms; the complementary plane corresponds to \((u-v)/\sqrt2\). Averaging cancels the off-diagonal Ricci block, and maximization separates the two Weyl blocks.

Set
\[
\zeta=(w_3^++w_3^--1/3)_+,\qquad
q=\frac13-2\beta.
\]
Equation (H), or (I) with \(\kappa=1/6\), gives
\[
\boxed{qP+\frac12\int|C|^2\le\int\zeta|Z|^2.} \tag{J}
\]

The maximum eigenvalue of the actual \(W_0\) is \(x^2/3\le1/3\). For a traceless symmetric \(3\times3\) matrix \(A\),
\(\lambda_{\max}(A)\le\sqrt{2/3}|A|\). Hence
\[
\zeta\le\sqrt{\frac23}\bigl(|W^+-W_0|+|W^-|\bigr).
\]
The weighted inequality
\[
(a+b)^2\le\frac43(a^2+3b^2)
\]
then gives, with \(B=\int|W^-|^2\),
\[
\boxed{\int\zeta^2\le\frac89(F+3B)
\le\frac89(D/18+3B).} \tag{K}
\]

For the balanced family, write \(U=3T_-/A\); here this agrees with the established \(U=3\min(T_+,T_-)/A\). With \(z=p/A-1\), the exact energy identities are
\[
D/18=2\pi^2A(e-1-h-2z),\qquad
B=\frac P3+\frac{2\pi^2A}{3}(U-e).
\]
They imply
\[
\boxed{D/18+3B=P+2\pi^2A(U-1-h-2z)=:\mathcal H.} \tag{L}
\]
This exact weighted cancellation is stronger than separately estimating \(D\) and \(B\).

If \(\alpha<4/7\), then \(q>0\). Equations (J)–(K) and Hölder give
\[
\boxed{
\int|Z|^4\ge\frac98q^2\frac{P^2}{\mathcal H},
\qquad
\|Z\|_{\infty,\mathrm{HS}}^2
\ge\frac98q^2\frac P{\mathcal H}.} \tag{M}
\]
Here \(\mathcal H>0\): otherwise (J)–(K) would contradict \(qP>0\).

Now take smooth attained minima on the balanced family with \(h\to0\). The known upper construction and I40 give
\[
\alpha\le\frac{4h}{1+h},\qquad P\gtrsim Ah,
\qquad U=1+h+O(h^2).
\]
Consequently
\[
\beta\le h,\qquad q\to1/3,\qquad
\mathcal H\le P+O(Ah^2)=P(1+O(h)),
\]
where \(z\ge0\) was retained with its favorable sign. Substitution in (M) proves
\[
\liminf\frac{\int|Z|^4}{P}\ge\frac18,
\qquad
\liminf\|Z\|_{\infty,\mathrm{HS}}^2\ge\frac18.
\]
Finally \(|Z|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le2|Z^\sharp|_{\mathrm{op}}\), proving the stated operator threshold \(1/(4\sqrt2)\).

4. What the ordinary equations still do not control

The decomposition also identifies the remaining signed term without asserting its smallness. Define
\[
L=2H-Q/8
=\frac23\int(1-x)^2(1+8x-2x^2)\ge0.
\]
Combining (A) with \(\Sigma=8K+Q+8J\) and Chern–Weil yields
\[
\boxed{
P-8\pi^2Ah
=2\left[2F+\Gamma+J+L+4\pi^2(p-A)-K\right].} \tag{N}
\]
Thus ordinary SW directly controls \(F,\Gamma,J,Q\) by \(D\), but the projective spinor gradient contribution \(K\) remains the possible negative payment in the sharp estimate.

For completeness, retaining the positive volume credit gives a sufficient condition weaker than demanding \(C_\omega=o(Ah)\). If \(\Delta V=V-2\pi^2A=O(Ah)\), then
\[
[K-\Gamma-J-L-4\pi^2(p-A)]_+=o(Ah)
\]
suffices for coefficient four. The exact necessary balance may retain the additional favorable term \(2F\). Neither balance has been proved generally.

All calculations were read-only. Clifford coefficients, polynomial factorizations, moment completion, and complementary-plane weights were checked symbolically; the ordinary decomposition and Cotton signs were also independently reviewed by the other agents.

## 418. 2026-09-27T10:03:43.493Z — variational_attainment_20260927e

Research thread: `01a0e248-bd1e-7621-9049-4b3a1af2e9f2`.

Two useful results are proved. No files were edited.

1. **A sharper uniform lifespan bound for conformal Ricci flow**

Let the balanced family satisfy the existing all-metric estimate
\[
\mathcal E(g)\ge c_1h,\qquad 0<c_1<4,
\]
and the actual scalar/Ricci budgets
\[
S_2\ge32\pi^2A,\qquad R\ge8\pi^2A(1+h).
\]
Write \(U=3T_-/A=1+h+O(h^2)\). Start from any scalar-\(-4\) metric with
\[
\mathcal E(g_0)\le\frac{4h}{1+h}.
\]

Use the classical conformal Ricci flow
\[
\partial_tg=-2Z-2\pi g,\qquad
(3\Delta+4)\pi=|Z|^2,\qquad Z=\operatorname{Ric}+g,
\]
where \(\Delta\ge0\). It preserves \(s=-4\). Short-time existence follows from [Lu–Qing–Zheng, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.5377), because \(3\Delta+4\) is invertible. Their equation (2.3), or direct integration of the pressure equation, gives
\[
V'=-4\int\pi=-P.
\]

Set
\[
V_* =2\pi^2A,\quad y=V/V_*,\quad p=P/V_*,
\quad \mu=c_1h,\quad \kappa=\frac{4\mu}{4-\mu}.
\]
Every smooth time satisfies
\[
y\ge1,\qquad y'=-p,\qquad
p\ge \max\left\{\kappa y,\;4(1+h-y),\;\frac43(y-U)\right\}. \tag{A}
\]
The three lower bounds come respectively from the all-metric defect gap, the absolute Ricci-energy bound, and
\[
P=\frac43V+4\int|W^-|^2-8\pi^2T_-.
\]
The initial upper defect bound implies \(p_0\le4hy_0\); combining this with the third wall gives
\[
y_0\le Y:=\frac{U}{1-3h}.
\]

For sufficiently small \(h\), the crossings of the three walls are ordered:
\[
1\le y_L=(1+h)(1-\mu/4)
\le y_H=\frac{U(4-\mu)}{4(1-\mu)}
\le Y.
\]
The decreasing wall controls \([1,y_L]\), the defect wall controls \([y_L,y_H]\), and the other-chirality wall controls \([y_H,Y]\). Integrating (A) proves that the maximal smooth existence time obeys
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{\max}\le {}&
\frac14\log\frac{4h}{(1+h)\mu}\\
&+\frac{4-\mu}{4\mu}
 \log\frac{U}{(1-\mu)(1+h)}\\
&+\frac34\log\frac{4h(1-\mu)}
 {\mu(1-3h)}. \tag{B}
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\boxed{\limsup_{h\to0}T_{\max}
\le 1+\log\frac4{c_1}.} \tag{C}
\]

This improves the simpler \(4/c_1+o(1)\) bound by using both energy walls. The middle interval contributes \(1+o(1)\); the other two contribute \(\frac14\log(4/c_1)\) and \(\frac34\log(4/c_1)\).

No pointwise pinching, energy-level preservation, stationarity, smooth attainment, or continuously selected SW solution is assumed along the flow. Each budget applies anew to the current metric on the same smooth manifold. The conclusion is loss of smooth continuation in this scalar normalization; it does not identify the singularity or itself exclude an attained minimizer.

There is also an exact evolution identity:
\[
P'=-2\langle\mathcal G_\tau,Z\rangle_{L^2}-\frac{P^2}{V}
=-2\int|\nabla Z|^2+4\int\operatorname{Rm}(Z,Z).
\]
The existing Cotton identity therefore yields
\[
P'\le-\frac23P-\int|C|^2+2\int\xi|Z|^2
\le
\left[-\frac23+
2\sqrt{\frac{8\mathcal H}{9P}}\|Z\|_\infty\right]P-\int|C|^2.
\]
The \(b=P/(4V)\) terms cancel exactly. This supplies actual short-time energy improvement for sufficiently pinched competitors, while (B) remains valid after that pinching is lost.

2. **An exact Hessian reduction: conformal directions cannot supply the missing instability**

Suppose \(g\) is a smooth \(\mathcal E\)-critical metric with \(s=-4\) and \(0<\alpha=\mathcal E(g)<1\). Put
\[
a=4-\alpha,\quad \tau=-1/a,\quad
c=\tau+\frac13=\frac{1-\alpha}{3(4-\alpha)}>0,
\]
and hold \(\tau\) fixed in every variation. Define
\[
L=3\Delta+4,\qquad M=a\Delta+4.
\]

For a transverse-traceless tensor \(k\), let
\[
\phi_0=\langle Z,k\rangle-\fint\langle Z,k\rangle.
\]
For mean-zero \(f\), the full defect Hessian satisfies
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hess}\mathcal E(k+2fg,k+2fg)
={}&\frac aR\left[
\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau(k,k)
-6c\,\langle\phi_0,\Delta L^{-1}\phi_0\rangle
\right]\\
&+\frac8R
\left\langle f-\tfrac12L^{-1}\phi_0,\,
LM\left(f-\tfrac12L^{-1}\phi_0\right)\right\rangle .
\end{aligned}} \tag{D}
\]

Here is the derivation. Conformal invariance of the Weyl integral and Chern–Gauss–Bonnet give
\[
Q_\tau=2\int|W|^2+cS_2-16\pi^2\chi.
\]
At constant scalar curvature,
\[
\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau(2fg,2fg)
=24c\langle f,\Delta Lf\rangle,
\]
and, at an actual critical metric,
\[
\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau(k,2fg)
=-12c\langle\phi_0,\Delta f\rangle .
\]
The scalar variation is
\[
(s'[k+2fg])_0=-\phi_0+2Lf.
\]
Using
\[
\mathcal E-J=\frac{S_2-S_1^2/V}{R},
\qquad J-\alpha=\frac aR Q_\tau,
\]
the Hessian is
\[
\operatorname{Hess}\mathcal E(h,h)
=\frac aR\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau(h,h)
+\frac2R\|(s'[h])_0\|_2^2.
\]
Completing the square proves (D).

In particular,
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Hess}\mathcal E(2fg,2fg)
=\frac8R\langle f,(3\Delta+4)((4-\alpha)\Delta+4)f\rangle>0
}
\]
for every nonzero mean-zero \(f\). The minimizing conformal correction in (D) is exactly the correction making the first scalar variation spatially constant.

Modulo diffeomorphisms and scaling, stability is therefore equivalent to nonnegativity of the reduced TT quadratic form
\[
\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau(k,k)
-6c\langle\phi_0,\Delta(3\Delta+4)^{-1}\phi_0\rangle. \tag{E}
\]
The correction is an explicit nonnegative operator of order zero:
\[
0\le \Delta(3\Delta+4)^{-1}<\frac13.
\]
The TT principal term of \(\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau\) is
\(\frac12\int|\Delta k|^2\), so approaching \(\tau=-1/4\) does not destroy ellipticity. Classical gauge ellipticity is consistent with [Gursky–Viaclovsky, Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1105.4648). Their Einstein Hessian formulas must not be substituted at these non-Einstein candidates.

One additional necessary condition follows by taking \(k=Z\):
\[
\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau(Z,Z)\ge
6c\,\frac{\lambda_1}{3\lambda_1+4}
\left(\int|Z|^4-\frac{P^2}{V}\right).
\]
Thus balanced smooth minimizers with \(\liminf\lambda_1\ge\ell>0\) would satisfy, using the existing Cotton concentration bound,
\[
\liminf
\frac{\operatorname{Hess}Q_\tau(Z,Z)}P
\ge\frac{\ell}{16(3\ell+4)}.
\]
This is a second-variation restriction, not a contradiction: the remaining TT Hessian has not been proved negative.

The crossing identities, the limit in (C), and the square completion in (D) were checked independently with exact SymPy algebra. Those checks support the displayed algebra; the analytic inputs remain the stated classical flow theorem and inherited all-metric budgets.

## 419. 2026-09-27T10:03:47.098Z — signed_spinor_balance_20260927e

Research thread: `01a0e248-5ab7-7ac0-8f2e-85adcae97664`.

A genuine closed countermodel shows that the stronger signed estimate in Section 4.5 cannot follow from the ordinary SW equations alone. It does **not** refute coefficient four on the balanced family: this example has \(h=0\), \(U=3\).

Write
\[
S:=K-\Gamma-J-L_0-4\pi^2(p-A).
\]
There is a smooth family of scalar-\(-4\) metrics with actual canonical SW solutions, on a fixed closed manifold, such that
\[
p=A=T_+,\qquad
S=K+O(\varepsilon^4)>0,
\qquad K=c\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^3),\quad c>0,
\]
while
\[
\Gamma,\ J,\ L_0=O(\varepsilon^4).
\]
Thus neither \(S\le0\) nor \(S_+=o(P+D_2)\) holds universally, even near a smooth KE metric, with nowhere-zero spinors and no degeneration.

The construction and verification are as follows.

1. **Fixed actual geometry and class.** Let
   \[
   (M,g_0)=(\Sigma_{g_1},g_1)\times(\Sigma_{g_2},g_2),
   \]
   where both closed surfaces have curvature \(-1\). Then
   \[
   \operatorname{Ric}_{g_0}=-g_0,\quad s=-4,\quad
   \Omega=\Omega_1+\Omega_2,\quad
   A=c_1(K_M^{-1})^2=T_+=8(g_1-1)(g_2-1).
   \]
   The canonical ordinary solution has parallel spinor \(\Phi_0\), \(|\Phi_0|^2=4\), and curvature \(\pm i\Omega\). Signs do not affect the calculations below.

2. **An explicit nonintegrable metric direction.** Choose a nonzero real holomorphic quadratic differential \(h_1\) on \(\Sigma_{g_1}\), interpreted as a trace-free, divergence-free symmetric tensor. Choose a nonconstant eigenfunction
   \[
   \Delta_{g_2}f=\lambda f,\qquad \lambda>0.
   \]
   Put \(H=f\,h_1\), extended by zero on all other product components, and \(B=g_0^{-1}H\). Then \(H\) is TT and \(BJ=-JB\). The metrics
   \[
   g_\varepsilon^{AK}(u,v)=g_0(e^{\varepsilon B}u,v)
   \]
   are positive, preserve \(\Omega\), and are \(\Omega\)-compatible. Their volume form is fixed.

   Take their scalar-\(-4\) Yamabe representatives
   \[
   \widehat g_\varepsilon=u_\varepsilon^2g_\varepsilon^{AK}.
   \]
   At \(\varepsilon=0\), the scalar variation is zero because \(H\) is TT and \(g_0\) is Einstein. Linearizing the normalized Yamabe equation gives
   \[
   (6\Delta+8)\dot u=0.
   \]
   Hence \(\dot u=0\), so \(\dot{\widehat g}=H\). Also, \(\Omega\) remains harmonic and self-dual after the conformal change. Consequently the canonical class satisfies
   \[
   p_\varepsilon=A
   \]
   exactly.

3. **Actual SW continuation, including regularity.** The canonical solution corresponds to the empty divisor. The Kähler monopole deformation description has tangent and obstruction spaces \(H^0(\mathcal O_D(D))\), \(H^1(\mathcal O_D(D))\), both zero for \(D=\varnothing\). Thus its gauge-fixed linearization is invertible. This is the classical input from [Okonek–Teleman, Theorem 3.1.2, pp. 413–414](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book37/files/okonek.pdf).

   The implicit function theorem therefore supplies a smooth branch of genuine ordinary SW solutions \((\mathcal A_\varepsilon,\Phi_\varepsilon)\) for \(\widehat g_\varepsilon\). No perturbed gauge equation is substituted.

   Under the natural spinor identification, the metric derivative of the Dirac equation consists of the term involving \(H\nabla_{\mathcal A_0}\Phi_0\) and the divergence/trace terms. All vanish here. The curvature-equation derivative contains only the trace term and the action of \(H\) on \(F_{\mathcal A_0}^{-}\); these also vanish. See [Scala, Theorem 3.3 and Section 4, pp. 1274–1276](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2640.pdf). In the fixed gauge slice,
   \[
   \dot{\mathcal A}=0,\qquad \dot\Phi=0.
   \]

4. **The positive signed term is a computed geometric effect.** Because \(B\) is anti-Hermitian, the first variation of the actual two-form \(\omega_\varepsilon=\sigma(\Phi_\varepsilon)\) is zero as an ordinary differential form. Therefore
   \[
   \rho_\varepsilon-4=O(\varepsilon^2),\qquad
   d\omega_\varepsilon=O(\varepsilon^2).
   \]
   The exact Dirac identity \(|\gamma|^2=4|d\omega|^2\) gives
   \(\Gamma=O(\varepsilon^4)\). Since the harmonic curvature representative remains \(\pm i\Omega\), \(J=O(\varepsilon^4)\). The amplitude polynomial gives \(L_0=O(\varepsilon^4)\).

   However, \(\nabla\omega\) has a nonzero first variation. The ordinary connection-variation formula gives
   \[
   \left|\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}
           \nabla^{\widehat g_\varepsilon}\Omega
          \right|_0\right|^2
      =\frac12|h_1|^2|df|^2.
   \]
   This includes all components: derivatives along the first surface cancel because every area-compatible surface metric preserves its area form; the displayed contribution comes from the mixed directions.

   The Hopf identity then yields
   \[
   K_\varepsilon
     =c\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^3),\qquad
   c=\frac14
      \left(\int_{\Sigma_{g_1}}|h_1|^2\right)
      \left(\int_{\Sigma_{g_2}}|df|^2\right)>0.
   \]
   Hence \(S_\varepsilon/K_\varepsilon\to1\).

There is also an explicit check of the compensation by \(F\). A trace-free Codazzi tensor on a curvature-\(-1\) surface satisfies the infinitesimal Einstein equation. Thus on the product,
\[
\dot Z=\frac{\lambda}{2}H,\qquad
P_\varepsilon=\lambda c\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^3).
\]
Applying the exact same-solution identity (4.16), with \(h=0\), gives
\[
\frac{P}{K}\longrightarrow\lambda,\qquad
\frac{F}{K}\longrightarrow\frac{\lambda+2}{4},\qquad
\frac{D_2}{K}\longrightarrow\frac92(\lambda+2).
\]
In particular
\[
\boxed{\frac{S_+}{P+D_2}\longrightarrow
                 \frac{2}{11\lambda+18}>0.}
\]
The retained square pays the positive signed term:
\[
2F-S=P/2.
\]
This is an actual smooth SW family, rather than a formal list of feasible moments.

A useful exact algebraic reduction also survives:
\[
\boxed{
S=T_\omega-\frac23\int(1-x^2)(1+2x^2)
       -J-4\pi^2(p-A).
}
\]
It follows directly from \(K=4\int x(1-x)\) and
\(\Gamma=8\int x^2(1-x)-T_\omega\). For Kähler-aligned solutions \(T_\omega=0\), so \(S\le0\), even for nonparallel vortex solutions. The countermodel identifies the missing positive contribution as actual nonintegrable directional variation.

The justified consequence for the balanced problem is limited but substantive: retain \(2F\) when pursuing the sharp estimate. The stronger sufficient target omitting it needs additional information from the balanced topology or minimizing geometry; it is not a general small-defect consequence of the same-solution Dirac–Weitzenböck system.

No files were edited. Exact polynomial cancellation and the mixed connection norm were checked symbolically; those checks supplement the analytic construction above.

## 420. 2026-09-27T10:07:14.707Z — core_extraction_20260927e

Research thread: `01a0e248-8704-79a0-9142-540e2c9978bc`.

Two usable results emerged. The first is a complete stationary endpoint obstruction with an explicit Sobolev hypothesis. The second genuinely extracts smooth complete cores from original curvature errors, but only under noncollapse and an absolute energy budget.

**1. A stationary endpoint gap on bounded topology**

Fix \(S,L,\Theta,T_0,\chi_0<\infty\). Consider closed oriented four-manifolds with

\[
s_g=-4,\qquad \chi(M)\le\chi_0,\qquad
0<T_+(M):=2\chi(M)+3\tau(M)\le T_0,
\]

whose metrics are exact critical points of

\[
Q_\theta(g)=\int|\operatorname{Ric}|^2+\theta\int s^2,
\qquad |\theta|\le\Theta.
\]

Assume the scale-invariant Sobolev inequality

\[
\left(\int |u|^4\right)^{1/2}
 \le S\int|du|^2+V^{-1/2}\int|u|^2.
\tag{A}
\]

For the manuscript’s \(Z_t\), every smooth self-dual form satisfying \(|\omega|\le L\), and every \(t\in[0,1/4]\), satisfy

\[
\boxed{\fint_M Z_t\ge c(S,L,\Theta,T_0,\chi_0)>0.}
\tag{B}
\]

No separate volume window, diameter bound or local \(L^p\) Ricci premise is needed.

Here is the complete argument.

Write \(z=\fint Z_t\), \(P=\int|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}|^2\), and \(W_+=\int|W^+|^2\), using the project’s endomorphism Hilbert–Schmidt Weyl convention. Since \(s=-4\),

\[
P=\int|\operatorname{Ric}+g|^2\le zV,
\]

and the bounded model satisfies

\[
W_+\le 2zV+\frac{L^4}{12}V.
\]

The exact closed Chern–Weil identity is

\[
4\pi^2T_+=2W_++\frac23V-\frac12P.
\tag{C}
\]

If \(z\le1/3\), this gives

\[
\boxed{\frac{4\pi^2}{2+L^4/6}\le V\le8\pi^2T_0.}
\tag{D}
\]

The lower bound uses the positive integer \(T_+\ge1\). Thus the volume window is derived before replacing normalized errors by absolute ones. The full four-index curvature norm obeys

\[
\int|\operatorname{Rm}|^2
 =32\pi^2\chi+4P
 \le32\pi^2\chi_0+\frac43(8\pi^2T_0).
\tag{E}
\]

Suppose (B) fails. After normalizing each metric to volume one, (A), (D), and (E) give uniform Sobolev and total curvature bounds. The required elliptic equation genuinely holds for every stated \(Q_\theta\)-critical metric:

\[
\Delta\operatorname{Ric}
=-2\operatorname{Rm}(\operatorname{Ric})
 -2\theta s\operatorname{Ric}
 +\frac12\bigl(|\operatorname{Ric}|^2+\theta s^2\bigr)g.
\tag{F}
\]

Every right-hand term is an algebraic \(\operatorname{Rm}*\operatorname{Ric}\) operation. Its coefficients are uniformly bounded for bounded \(\theta\). There is no division by \(\theta+1/3\); consequently the argument includes \(\theta=-1/3\) when constant scalar curvature is imposed.

Equation (F) is checked directly against [Catino, §2, equation (2.1) and Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1404.0569). [Anderson, Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 3.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312111) provide orbifold compactness and smooth regular charts for this elliptic system under the stated Sobolev control. Remark 3.10 explicitly discusses other quadratic curvature critical metrics. This is not an invocation of Einstein compactness for the original metrics.

Return to the physical scale using the convergent volume factors from (D). On a nonempty regular chart the metrics converge smoothly. Since \(z_jV_j\to0\), their limit satisfies \(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\). The self-dual form estimate

\[
\|\omega_j\|_{H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}}
 \le C\bigl(\|d\omega_j\|_{2}+\|\omega_j\|_2\bigr)
\]

gives a subsequential limiting closed self-dual form with squared norm two. The amplitude bound makes the quadratic models converge strongly in \(L^2\). Hence

\[
W^+=t_\infty\left(\frac23I-\omega\otimes\omega\right),
\qquad t_\infty\in[0,1/4].
\]

This is exactly the local configuration already excluded in I45: Armstrong’s local obstruction at \(t=0\), and the Einstein Bianchi argument forcing \(t=1/2\) when \(t>0\). The contradiction proves (B).

Consequences and limits:

- An actual csc quadratic-critical endpoint sequence on a fixed topology must lose uniform control of (A).
- This is an alternative to I48’s small local lower-Ricci budget. That budget has not been derived.
- The conclusion concerns stationary metrics. Yamabe representatives or arbitrary minimizing sequences need not satisfy (F).
- It covers \(\beta\ge4\), not the \(\beta=2\) sharp-coefficient problem.
- Its uniformity requires bounds on \(T_+\) and \(\chi\) themselves, not merely \(\chi/T_+\).

**2. Actual smooth-core extraction at maximal curvature**

A separate geometric statement does not assume a pre-existing neck or decomposition.

Let \(g_j\) be exact csc \(Q_{\theta_j}\)-critical metrics, with \(|\theta_j|\le\Theta\), satisfying

\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{g_j} B_s(x)\ge v\,s^4
 \quad(0<s\le r_0,\ \text{all }x),
\qquad
\int|\operatorname{Rm}_{g_j}|^2\le E,
\tag{G}
\]

and let \(|\omega_j|\le L,\ t_j\in[0,1/4]\). Assume the absolute original curvature errors tend to zero:

\[
\int\left(
 |\operatorname{Ric}_{g_j}+g_j|^2+
 |W^+_{g_j}-A_{\omega_j,t_j}|^2
 \right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{H}
\]

If \(Q_j=\max_M|\operatorname{Rm}_{g_j}|\to\infty\), choose maximum points \(x_j\) and put

\[
r_j=Q_j^{-1/2},\qquad h_j=r_j^{-2}g_j.
\]

Then, after passage to a subsequence,

\[
(M_j,h_j,x_j)\longrightarrow(X,h,x_\infty)
\]

smoothly on compact subsets, where \(X\) is a smooth complete, nonflat, Ricci-flat, anti-self-dual ALE four-manifold.

The derivation is as follows.

1. By construction, \(|\operatorname{Rm}_{h_j}|\le1\) and its value at \(x_j\) is one. Condition (G) supplies noncollapse on every fixed rescaled ball.
2. Bounded rescaled curvature supplies local upper volume bounds. Sufficiently small fixed rescaled balls therefore have curvature energy below the regularity threshold.
3. [Tian–Viaclovsky, Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0612491) applies to the general system \(\Delta\operatorname{Ric}=\operatorname{Rm}*\operatorname{Ric}\) under lower volume growth. It yields uniform curvature derivative estimates. Together with bounded curvature and noncollapse, these give smooth pointed compactness and completeness.
4. On each fixed rescaled ball, original volume is \(O(r_j^4)\). Scale invariance of curvature-square integrals and (H) imply \(\operatorname{Ric}_h=0\). The bounded Weyl model disappears under rescaling, so \(W_h^+=0\).
5. The limit has finite curvature energy and Euclidean lower volume growth. Only now is the Ricci-flat Bando–Kasue–Nakajima ALE theorem applicable. The needed statement is Theorem 1.5 of [Bando–Kasue–Nakajima](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01389045): maximal volume growth and finite critical curvature energy give ALE asymptotics; in dimension four the order is four. This is also explicitly restated in [Buzano–Yudowitz, Theorem 2.7](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00209-023-03272-z).

Choose a sufficiently large compact ALE truncation \(K_R\subset X\). Smooth convergence embeds \(K_R\) into \(M_j\), producing actual smooth one-boundary cores \(\Omega_j\). Their original volumes tend to zero. Their lifted outer collars become as close to a flat cone as desired by first choosing \(R\) large and then \(j\) large. Thus these are precisely whole smooth cores to which I47 applies.

Moreover,

\[
\int_{\Omega_j}
\left(|\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}|^2+4|W^+|^2+s^2/12\right)\longrightarrow0,
\]

because (H) tends to zero and the bounded background terms multiply \(\operatorname{Vol}(\Omega_j)\to0\). Therefore their oriented infinity group cannot be any nontrivial \(1/n(1,-2)\): I47 would force its uniform positive cost.

The group is also nontrivial, since a smooth Ricci-flat ALE space with trivial infinity group is Euclidean by Bishop–Gromov equality, contradicting the normalized curvature at the base point. Noncollapse gives

\[
|\Gamma|\le\omega_4/v.
\]

Consequently only finitely many marked group/lift types occur, so I46’s finite-family constants apply to the extracted annuli.

The remaining analytic loss is precise. The rescaled amplitude error is

\[
r_j^{-4}\int_{\Omega_j}(\rho-\rho_\beta)^2,
\]

and the rescaled opposite-spinor residual has factor \(r_j^{-8/3}\). Absolute errors tending to zero do not make these quantities vanish. Thus the extracted ALE core need not retain the nonzero calibrated opposite spinor. This prevents combining extraction and the faithful-determinant argument into an unconditional contradiction.

These are terminal ALE cores produced at maximum curvature. The argument does not identify them with the entire exceptional/handle surgery region, produce a complete bubble tree, or prove that all relevant topology lies inside them. It therefore complements the root’s whole-surgery-core observation without supplying the missing marking.
